principles - - - - - - - - - - 1. single source of truth : all audit - producing services must emit a canonical event envelope with standard header fields ( see event header below ). 2. minimal required fields : each event must contain the required fields ; optional fields must be populated when available. 3. versioning policy : major. minor. patch semantic versioning for schema ( v1. 0. 0 ). minor / patch changes are backward - compatible ; major changes require migration plan and cross - team sign - off. 4. evidence tagging : every event intended for compliance / forensics must carry evidence tags that drive retention and access controls. 5. privacy - first : sensitive payloads must never be stored in plain text. use pointer - to - encr

    "content": "{\n  \"thread_id\": \"thread-20260712-priya-residency-0147\",\n  \"mailbox_owner\": \"priya_natarajan\",\n  \"subject\": \"Regional data residency & fallback playbook for FinServ RFP\",\n  \"participants_internal\": [\n    \"priya_natarajan\",\n    \"karthik_iyer\",\n    \"marissa_cole\",\n    \"jonas_weber\"\n  ],\n  \"participants_external\": [\n    \"Lucia Martin <lucia.martin@finservglobal.com>\",\n    \"FinServ Global Procurement <procurement@finservglobal.com>\"\n  ],\n  \"message_count\": \"6\",\n  \"first_email_at\": \"2026-06-30T14:03:00+01:00\",\n  \"last_email_at\": \"2026-07-12T10:22:00-07:00\",\n  \"thread_type\": \"security_compliance\",\n  \"related_account\": \"FinServ Global\",\n  \"deal_id\": \"RDW-2026-4621\",\n  \"region\": \"eu\",\n  \"has_attachments\": \"true\",\n  \"attachments\": [\n    \"20260701-residency-matrix.xlsx\",\n    \"RFP-Response-FinServ-Redwood-20260712.pdf\"\n  ],\n  \"related_links\": [\n    \"https://drive.redwood.ai/finserv/rfp-residency-202607\",\n    \"https://app.docusign.com/some-docu-sign-link/FinServ-RDW-SLA-exception\"\n  ],\n  \"messages\": [\n    \"From: Lucia Martin <lucia.martin@finservglobal.com>\\\\nTo: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>\\\\nDate: 2026-06-30T14:03:00+01:00\\\\nSubject: Data residency requirements for upcoming procurement - FinServ RFP\\\\n\\\\nHi Priya,\\\\n\\\\nThanks for the call earlier. As we prepare the formal RFP response, procurement has asked for a concise matrix that confirms:\\\\n- Whether customer data can be resident in EU-only regions (data at rest and logs).\\\\n- Where the control plane/management console lives and whether it can be located outside EU.\\\\n- Options for KMS/HSM key storage (customer-managed keys by region).\\\\n- Fallback behavior when primary EU capacity is constrained (does data move, is processing denied, or is there an opt-in routing to another region?).\\\\n- Audit log locations and retention controls.\\\\n\\\\nCan you share a short operational playbook and a matrix by 2026-07-12 so we can include it in the procurement package? Also note procurement will require a short paragraph we can include in the contract about guaranteed regional placement and any exceptions.\\\\n\\\\nAppreciate it,\\\\nLucia\\\\nLucia Martin\\\\nDirector, Cloud Architecture\\\\nFinServ Global\\\\n[Attachment: FinServ_RFP_Scope.pdf (pdf)]\",\n    \"From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>\\\\nTo: Lucia Martin <lucia.martin@finservglobal.com>\\\\nCc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>\\\\nDate: 2026-07-01T09:15:00-07:00\\\\nSubject: Re: Data residency requirements for upcoming procurement - FinServ RFP\\\\n\\\\nHi Lucia \\u2014 thanks, we can do that. I attached a first-pass matrix that maps our deployment and controls to the items you listed. Highlights up front:\\\\n- EU-resident data: supported via Dedicated and Private deployments; hosted API supports EU-only tenancy when requested (see matrix rows).\\\\n- Control plane: default hosted control plane is multi-region; Private customers can run control plane in their VPC.\\\\n- KMS/HSM: customer-managed KMS with region-scoped keys is supported for Private; hosted offers KMS integration and can pin key residency.\\\\n- Fallback: we offer configurable routing policies \\u2014 options are deny, replicate to another pinned region (with explicit consent), or route to a compatibility model in a non-EU region with redaction flags.\\\\n\\\\nPlease see attached: 20260701-residency-matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet) and a short playbook we will expand. I'll loop in engineering and security to tighten the wording before 7/12.\\\\n\\\\nNext steps: I'll follow up internally and send the final playbook + contract paragraph by 7/12.\\\\n\\\\nRegards,\\\\nPriya Natarajan\\\\nSr. Account Executive, EMEA\\\\nRedwood Inference\\\\n[Attachment: 20260701-residency-matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet)]\",\n    \"From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>\\\\nTo: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>\\\\nDate: 2026-07-02T11:28:00-07:00\\\\nSubject: Fwd: Data residency requirements for upcoming procurement - need technical + legal wording\\\\n\\\\nTeam \\u2014 forwarding Lucia's ask and the draft matrix. Can you each review for the following and suggest exact wording we can give procurement:\\\\n1) A 2-3 sentence contract paragraph that states what \\\"EU resident\\\" means for Redwood (control plane vs data plane vs audit logs).\\\\n2) Clear bullet list of fallback behaviors with default and opt-in options (what triggers each, and how we document consent).\\\\n3) Specifics on KMS/HSM: what we can and cannot guarantee for hosted tenancy vs Private (VPC).\\\\n\\\\nMarissa, please focus on audit logs/retention language. Karthik, please validate the technical behaviors (KV cache, model artifacts, replication). Jonas, add an operational note for onboarding (time-to-pin region, testing checklist).\\\\n\\\\nThanks \\u2014 Priya\\\\n\\\\nOn Tue, Jun 30, 2026 at 14:03 Lucia Martin <lucia.martin@finservglobal.com> wrote:\\\\n> ... (original message quoted) ...\",\n    \"From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>\\\\nTo: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>\\\\nDate: 2026-07-06T16:42:00-07:00\\\\nSubject: Re: Fwd: Data residency requirements for upcoming procurement - need technical + legal wording\\\\n\\\\nFolks \\u2014 draft technical language below (feel free to copy/paste into the playbook). I also attached an updated residency matrix with column-level detail for logs, keys, and model artifacts.\\\\n\\\\nA. Definitions (copy-ready):\\\\n- \\\\\\\"EU-resident customer data\\\\\\\": customer-provided inputs, generated outputs, and metadata persisted in storage that are written to a storage tier physically located within an EU region selected at onboarding.\\\\n- \\\\\\\"Control plane\\\\\\\": service management endpoints (API, console) that may be hosted outside the EU for hosted customers; for Private deployments, control plane can be provisioned in-customer VPC (EU region) upon request.\\\\n\\\\nB. Deployment & guarantees:\\\\n- Hosted (default): Customer data storage can be pinned to EU regions; control plane is global by default but may be restricted via Private offer. Audit logs for hosted customers are stored in region of record; retention configurable but short-term trace logs are replicated for reliability (replicas are tagged and access-controlled).\\\\n- Dedicated / Private: Full EU residency for data, logs, and keys. Customer-managed KMS/HSM supported; Redwood will not have access to customer-managed keys.\\\\n\\\\nC. KMS/HSM specifics:\\\\n- Hosted: Redwood integrates with customer KMS providers (KMS calls proxied); key material is stored per the KMS vendor region. We can accept a contractual requirement to keep keys in EU for EU-residency customers.\\\\n- Private: You hold keys in your KMS/HSM; we provide integration guidance and an operational checklist for key rotation and audits.\\\\n\\\\nD. Fallback strategies (ordered):\\\\n1) Soft-deny + queuing: if EU capacity is saturated, requests are queued for configurable time (customer sets time-to-wait) and not routed out of region.\\\\n2) Explicit opt-in cross-region routing: with documented consent, traffic can be routed to a secondary region (US/APAC) to complete processing; data is tagged and access controls applied.\\\\n3) Model-variant routing (latency-first): route to an equivalent, lower-capacity model hosted in EU-friendly compatible infra; no data egress.\\\\n4) Emergency regional failover: with prior contractual agreement, replicate operational state to a pre-approved non-EU region for defined duration (requires DocuSign SLA exception).\\\\n\\\\nE. Logs & audit:\\\\n- Audit logs for data access are retained in-region by default; customers can request longer retention or cross-region replication for analytics (explicit opt-in).\\\\n- We provide regular SOC2-aligned attestations and a read-only audit export that can be pushed to customer S3/GCS in a pinned region.\\\\n\\\\nOperational notes (Jonas): onboarding to pin an EU region typically takes 5-10 business days for Dedicated; Private onboarding varies by network setup. See matrix for exact timelines.\\\\n\\\\nAttachment: updated matrix: 20260706-residency-matrix-updated.xlsx\\\\n\\\\n-Karthik\\\\nStaff Software Engineer, Inference Infrastructure\\\\nRedwood Inference\",\n    \"From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>\\\\nTo: Lucia Martin <lucia.martin@finservglobal.com>, FinServ Global Procurement <procurement@finservglobal.com>\\\\nCc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>\\\\nDate: 2026-07-10T08:17:00-07:00\\\\nSubject: Regional residency playbook + contract paragraph (FinServ RFP)\\\\n\\\\nHi Lucia \\u2014 attached is the finalized playbook and the short contract paragraph for procurement. Key excerpts below for quick review: \\\\n\\\\nContract paragraph (suggested):\\\\n\\\\\\\"Redwood Inference will store Customer Data (inputs, outputs, and persistent metadata) within the EU region selected at onboarding. The control plane may be hosted outside the EU for Hosted customers; customers electing Private or Dedicated deployment models may request the control plane be provisioned within their EU region. Cross-region processing or temporary replication will only occur with Customer's prior written consent or per an executed SLA exception. KMS keys used for encryption at rest will be maintained in the Customer-specified region where Customer provides or configures regional key management.\\\\\\\"\\\\n\\\\nOperational summary (one-line bullets):\\\\n- EU-resident data: supported via Dedicated and Private; hosted tenancy supports region pinning.\\\\n- Default fallback: soft-deny + queuing (configurable) to avoid involuntary egress.\\\\n- Opt-in fallback: explicit cross-region routing or documented emergency failover (requires SLA exception).\\\\n- KMS: customer-managed keys supported; we will integrate with region-scoped keys.\\\\n\\\\nAttachments: RFP-Response-FinServ-Redwood-20260712.pdf (playbook) and 20260701-residency-matrix.xlsx (detailed matrix).\\\\n\\\\nPlease confirm if procurement would like the SLA exception draft now \\u2014 I can route it for DocuSign. Suggested next step: procurement approves paragraph and we add the SLA exception as an appendix to the agreement.\\\\n\\\\nThanks,\\\\nPriya\\\\nSr. Account Executive, EMEA\\\\nRedwood Inference\\\\n[Attachment: RFP-Response-FinServ-Redwood-20260712.pdf (pdf)]\",\n    \"From: Lucia Martin <lucia.martin@finservglobal.com>\\\\nTo: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>\\\\nCc: FinServ Global Procurement <procurement@finservglobal.com>\\\\nDate: 2026-07-12T10:22:00-07:00\\\\nSubject: Re: Regional residency playbook + contract paragraph (FinServ RFP)\\\\n\\\\nHi Priya \\u2014 this is perfect, thanks to you and the team. Procurement is happy with the contract paragraph and the operational bullets. Two quick items: \\\\n1) We need a one-sentence line for the SOW that calls out max queue wait before failover (we propose 30 seconds by default).\\\\n2) Procurement would like the SLA exception drafted now so legal can review in parallel with the PO.\\\\n\\\\nPlease send the DocuSign link when ready and confirm the SOW line. If you can provide a short redlined SLA appendix in the DocuSign package, that will speed things up.\\\\n\\\\nI'll put the PO timeline on hold until we have the final doc.\\\\n\\\\nBest,\\\\nLucia\\\\nDirector, Cloud Architecture\\\\nFinServ Global\"\n  ],\n  \"title_field_name\": \"subject\",\n  \"content_field_names\": [\n    \"messages\"\n  ],\n  \"dataset_doc_uuid\": \"dsid_2b023bf742d74ad598bc190502d98808\"\n}",

  "thread_id": "thread-20260712-priya-residency-0147",
  "mailbox_owner": "priya_natarajan",
  "subject": "Regional data residency & fallback playbook for FinServ RFP",
  "participants_internal": [
    "priya_natarajan",
    "karthik_iyer",
    "marissa_cole",
    "jonas_weber"
  ],
  "participants_external": [
    "Lucia Martin <lucia.martin@finservglobal.com>",
    "FinServ Global Procurement <procurement@finservglobal.com>"
  ],
  "message_count": "6",
  "first_email_at": "2026-06-30T14:03:00+01:00",
  "last_email_at": "2026-07-12T10:22:00-07:00",
  "thread_type": "security_compliance",
  "related_account": "FinServ Global",
  "deal_id": "RDW-2026-4621",
  "region": "eu",
  "has_attachments": "true",
  "attachments": [
    "20260701-residency-matrix.xlsx",
    "RFP-Response-FinServ-Redwood-20260712.pdf"
  ],
  "related_links": [
    "https://drive.redwood.ai/finserv/rfp-residency-202607",
    "https://app.docusign.com/some-docu-sign-link/FinServ-RDW-SLA-exception"
  ],
  "messages": [
    "From: Lucia Martin <lucia.martin@finservglobal.com>\\nTo: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>\\nDate: 2026-06-30T14:03:00+01:00\\nSubject: Data residency requirements for upcoming procurement - FinServ RFP\\n\\nHi Priya,\\n\\nThanks for the call earlier. As we prepare the formal RFP response, procurement has asked for a concise matrix that confirms:\\n- Whether customer data can be resident in EU-only regions (data at rest and logs).\\n- Where the control plane/management console lives and whether it can be located outside EU.\\n- Options for KMS/HSM key storage (customer-managed keys by region).\\n- Fallback behavior when primary EU capacity is constrained (does data move, is processing denied, or is there an opt-in routing to another region?).\\n- Audit log locations and retention controls.\\n\\nCan you share a short operational playbook and a matrix by 2026-07-12 so we can include it in the procurement package? Also note procurement will require a short paragraph we can include in the contract about guaranteed regional placement and any exceptions.\\n\\nAppreciate it,\\nLucia\\nLucia Martin\\nDirector, Cloud Architecture\\nFinServ Global\\n[Attachment: FinServ_RFP_Scope.pdf (pdf)]",
    "From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>\\nTo: Lucia Martin <lucia.martin@finservglobal.com>\\nCc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>\\nDate: 2026-07-01T09:15:00-07:00\\nSubject: Re: Data residency requirements for upcoming procurement - FinServ RFP\\n\\nHi Lucia \u2014 thanks, we can do that. I attached a first-pass matrix that maps our deployment and controls to the items you listed. Highlights up front:\\n- EU-resident data: supported via Dedicated and Private deployments; hosted API supports EU-only tenancy when requested (see matrix rows).\\n- Control plane: default hosted control plane is multi-region; Private customers can run control plane in their VPC.\\n- KMS/HSM: customer-managed KMS with region-scoped keys is supported for Private; hosted offers KMS integration and can pin key residency.\\n- Fallback: we offer configurable routing policies \u2014 options are deny, replicate to another pinned region (with explicit consent), or route to a compatibility model in a non-EU region with redaction flags.\\n\\nPlease see attached: 20260701-residency-matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet) and a short playbook we will expand. I'll loop in engineering and security to tighten the wording before 7/12.\\n\\nNext steps: I'll follow up internally and send the final playbook + contract paragraph by 7/12.\\n\\nRegards,\\nPriya Natarajan\\nSr. Account Executive, EMEA\\nRedwood Inference\\n[Attachment: 20260701-residency-matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet)]",
    "From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>\\nTo: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>\\nDate: 2026-07-02T11:28:00-07:00\\nSubject: Fwd: Data residency requirements for upcoming procurement - need technical + legal wording\\n\\nTeam \u2014 forwarding Lucia's ask and the draft matrix. Can you each review for the following and suggest exact wording we can give procurement:\\n1) A 2-3 sentence contract paragraph that states what \"EU resident\" means for Redwood (control plane vs data plane vs audit logs).\\n2) Clear bullet list of fallback behaviors with default and opt-in options (what triggers each, and how we document consent).\\n3) Specifics on KMS/HSM: what we can and cannot guarantee for hosted tenancy vs Private (VPC).\\n\\nMarissa, please focus on audit logs/retention language. Karthik, please validate the technical behaviors (KV cache, model artifacts, replication). Jonas, add an operational note for onboarding (time-to-pin region, testing checklist).\\n\\nThanks \u2014 Priya\\n\\nOn Tue, Jun 30, 2026 at 14:03 Lucia Martin <lucia.martin@finservglobal.com> wrote:\\n> ... (original message quoted) ...",
    "From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>\\nTo: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>\\nDate: 2026-07-06T16:42:00-07:00\\nSubject: Re: Fwd: Data residency requirements for upcoming procurement - need technical + legal wording\\n\\nFolks \u2014 draft technical language below (feel free to copy/paste into the playbook). I also attached an updated residency matrix with column-level detail for logs, keys, and model artifacts.\\n\\nA. Definitions (copy-ready):\\n- \\\"EU-resident customer data\\\": customer-provided inputs, generated outputs, and metadata persisted in storage that are written to a storage tier physically located within an EU region selected at onboarding.\\n- \\\"Control plane\\\": service management endpoints (API, console) that may be hosted outside the EU for hosted customers; for Private deployments, control plane can be provisioned in-customer VPC (EU region) upon request.\\n\\nB. Deployment & guarantees:\\n- Hosted (default): Customer data storage can be pinned to EU regions; control plane is global by default but may be restricted via Private offer. Audit logs for hosted customers are stored in region of record; retention configurable but short-term trace logs are replicated for reliability (replicas are tagged and access-controlled).\\n- Dedicated / Private: Full EU residency for data, logs, and keys. Customer-managed KMS/HSM supported; Redwood will not have access to customer-managed keys.\\n\\nC. KMS/HSM specifics:\\n- Hosted: Redwood integrates with customer KMS providers (KMS calls proxied); key material is stored per the KMS vendor region. We can accept a contractual requirement to keep keys in EU for EU-residency customers.\\n- Private: You hold keys in your KMS/HSM; we provide integration guidance and an operational checklist for key rotation and audits.\\n\\nD. Fallback strategies (ordered):\\n1) Soft-deny + queuing: if EU capacity is saturated, requests are queued for configurable time (customer sets time-to-wait) and not routed out of region.\\n2) Explicit opt-in cross-region routing: with documented consent, traffic can be routed to a secondary region (US/APAC) to complete processing; data is tagged and access controls applied.\\n3) Model-variant routing (latency-first): route to an equivalent, lower-capacity model hosted in EU-friendly compatible infra; no data egress.\\n4) Emergency regional failover: with prior contractual agreement, replicate operational state to a pre-approved non-EU region for defined duration (requires DocuSign SLA exception).\\n\\nE. Logs & audit:\\n- Audit logs for data access are retained in-region by default; customers can request longer retention or cross-region replication for analytics (explicit opt-in).\\n- We provide regular SOC2-aligned attestations and a read-only audit export that can be pushed to customer S3/GCS in a pinned region.\\n\\nOperational notes (Jonas): onboarding to pin an EU region typically takes 5-10 business days for Dedicated; Private onboarding varies by network setup. See matrix for exact timelines.\\n\\nAttachment: updated matrix: 20260706-residency-matrix-updated.xlsx\\n\\n-Karthik\\nStaff Software Engineer, Inference Infrastructure\\nRedwood Inference",
    "From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>\\nTo: Lucia Martin <lucia.martin@finservglobal.com>, FinServ Global Procurement <procurement@finservglobal.com>\\nCc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>\\nDate: 2026-07-10T08:17:00-07:00\\nSubject: Regional residency playbook + contract paragraph (FinServ RFP)\\n\\nHi Lucia \u2014 attached is the finalized playbook and the short contract paragraph for procurement. Key excerpts below for quick review: \\n\\nContract paragraph (suggested):\\n\\\"Redwood Inference will store Customer Data (inputs, outputs, and persistent metadata) within the EU region selected at onboarding. The control plane may be hosted outside the EU for Hosted customers; customers electing Private or Dedicated deployment models may request the control plane be provisioned within their EU region. Cross-region processing or temporary replication will only occur with Customer's prior written consent or per an executed SLA exception. KMS keys used for encryption at rest will be maintained in the Customer-specified region where Customer provides or configures regional key management.\\\"\\n\\nOperational summary (one-line bullets):\\n- EU-resident data: supported via Dedicated and Private; hosted tenancy supports region pinning.\\n- Default fallback: soft-deny + queuing (configurable) to avoid involuntary egress.\\n- Opt-in fallback: explicit cross-region routing or documented emergency failover (requires SLA exception).\\n- KMS: customer-managed keys supported; we will integrate with region-scoped keys.\\n\\nAttachments: RFP-Response-FinServ-Redwood-20260712.pdf (playbook) and 20260701-residency-matrix.xlsx (detailed matrix).\\n\\nPlease confirm if procurement would like the SLA exception draft now \u2014 I can route it for DocuSign. Suggested next step: procurement approves paragraph and we add the SLA exception as an appendix to the agreement.\\n\\nThanks,\\nPriya\\nSr. Account Executive, EMEA\\nRedwood Inference\\n[Attachment: RFP-Response-FinServ-Redwood-20260712.pdf (pdf)]",
    "From: Lucia Martin <lucia.martin@finservglobal.com>\\nTo: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>\\nCc: FinServ Global Procurement <procurement@finservglobal.com>\\nDate: 2026-07-12T10:22:00-07:00\\nSubject: Re: Regional residency playbook + contract paragraph (FinServ RFP)\\n\\nHi Priya \u2014 this is perfect, thanks to you and the team. Procurement is happy with the contract paragraph and the operational bullets. Two quick items: \\n1) We need a one-sentence line for the SOW that calls out max queue wait before failover (we propose 30 seconds by default).\\n2) Procurement would like the SLA exception drafted now so legal can review in parallel with the PO.\\n\\nPlease send the DocuSign link when ready and confirm the SOW line. If you can provide a short redlined SLA appendix in the DocuSign package, that will speed things up.\\n\\nI'll put the PO timeline on hold until we have the final doc.\\n\\nBest,\\nLucia\\nDirector, Cloud Architecture\\nFinServ Global"
  ],

    "id": "dsid_8bcf38423f3548078433c0dd4de38b36",

    "title": "EU Tenant Routing Authorization Matrix and Residency Enforcement",
    "source": "EnterpriseRAG/linear",
    "content": "{\n  \"key\": \"ENG-100721\",\n  \"team\": \"engineering\",\n  \"title\": \"EU Tenant Routing Authorization Matrix and Residency Enforcement\",\n  \"status\": \"In Progress\",\n  \"priority\": \"P1\",\n  \"created_at\": \"2026-03-10\",\n  \"updated_at\": \"2026-03-12\",\n  \"creator\": \"Aisha Patel\",\n  \"assignee\": \"Marco Rivera\",\n  \"project\": \"geo-compliance-routing\",\n  \"cycle\": \"2026-W11\",\n  \"estimate\": \"8\",\n  \"due_date\": \"2026-03-28\",\n  \"labels\": [\n    \"geo-routing\",\n    \"residency\",\n    \"policy-engine\",\n    \"privacy\"\n  ],\n  \"dependencies\": [\n    \"ENG-52340\",\n    \"ENG-81234\"\n  ],\n  \"customer_impact\": \"high\",\n  \"release\": \"routing-2.4\",\n  \"security_review_required\": \"true\",\n  \"description\": \"Implement a tenant-scoped authorization matrix and enforcement layer that guarantees EU-only data residency and routing for customers that opt into or require EU restrictions. This ticket defines the policy precedence, tenant configuration schema, routing decision flow, runtime enforcement hooks, audit logging, and rollout strategy. The goal is to provide deterministic, auditable routing decisions (region + tier + model variant) that satisfy legal/regulatory EU residency constraints and customer allowlist/denylist controls.\",\n  \"spec\": \"Overview:\\nWe will add a Tenant Routing Authorization Matrix (TRAM) that is evaluated at request ingress and used by the Smart Routing engine. TRAM is tenant-scoped (applies to org or project depending on tenant_id) and supports multiple policy axes: residency_constraints (enum: eu_only, any_region, region_allowlist), allowed_tiers (list: hosted,dedicated,private), model_variant_preference (map: role->preferred_variant), and explicit_customer_allow/deny lists for special routing exceptions. Policy precedence: explicit denylist > tenant residency enforcement > per-route overrides (if permitted) > global defaults.\\n\\nRouting decision flow (high level):\\n1) Ingress: request arrives with tenant_id and metadata (consent_header, jurisdiction_hint, route_id).\\n2) Resolve tenant TRAM config from tenant-config cache (fast-path). If missing, call Tenant Policy Service with cache miss metric.\\n3) Evaluate compliance predicates: does request require EU residency? Is tenant in EU-only mode? Is the requested route marked as cross-border-allowed?\\n4) Candidate pool selection: choose model variants and deployment regions matching allowed_tiers and residency constraints. If no candidate satisfies strict residency, move to fallback policy (see fallback section).\\n5) Authorization check: consult tenant-level allowlist/denylist for special customer exceptions (IP/routing tags).\\n6) Finalize decision, annotate request trace, and forward to Serving Runtime via routing API.\\n\\nFallback policy:\\n- Strict mode (tenant residency_constraints == eu_only AND fail_on_violation==true): reject request with 403 and audit log.\\n- Soft mode (default): fallback to EU-compatible model variant in hosted or dedicated EU pool. If none available, route to degraded model with redaction tag and notify customer via header X-Redwood-Routing-Fallback. Telemetry increments fallback_used.\\n\\nPolicy update semantics:\\n- TRAM updates are versioned. Each change creates a policy_version id.\",\n  \"api_changes\": \"New endpoints and headers:\\n- GET /v1/tenant/{tenant_id}/tram -> returns current TRAM config and policy_version.\\n- POST /internal/routing/decide -> internal API used by edge to request decision; payload: {tenant_id, route_id, jurisdiction_hint, consent_header, preferred_zone}. Response: {decision_id, region, tier, model_variant, policy_version, reason}.\\n- New response headers for routed requests: X-Redwood-Routing-Decision, X-Redwood-Policy-Version, X-Redwood-Routing-Fallback (when applicable).\\nAuth: internal endpoints require mTLS and service-to-service JWT with scope: routing:decide.\\nBackwards compatibility: default when tenant has no TRAM is legacy routing behavior; feature flag 'tram-enforce' will gate enforcement during rollout.\",\n  \"data_model_changes\": \"Tenant config storage (KV store + DB index):\\n- New table/collection 'tenant_tram' with columns (tenant_id, residency_constraints, allowed_tiers, model_variant_map, allowlist, denylist, fail_on_violation, policy_version, updated_by, updated_at).\\n- Cache key: tram:{tenant_id}:{policy_version}.\\n- Audit logs: each routing decision writes a compact audit record to routing_audit (decision_id, tenant_id, timestamp, decision, reason, policy_version, route_id, request_id).\\nNote: Use existing config migration tooling; add DB migration script and store initial policy_version = 1 when creating TRAM entries.\",\n  \"rollout_plan\": \"Phase 1 - Canaries (2 weeks):\\n- Enable read-only TRAM on edge to record decisions and diffs; do not enforce. Collect mismatch_count metric.\\n- Target 5% of tenants (low-risk) + 100% of EU-region traffic for visibility.\\n\\nPhase 2 - Soft enforcement (2 weeks):\\n- Enable soft mode for 20% tenants. Fallback to EU-compatible variants and emit headers. Add customer notifications for impacted tenants.\\n\\nPhase 3 - Strict enforcement (gradual):\\n- Opt-in tenants can flip to strict mode. After 1 month of low mismatch, enable strict mode for customers who have completed verification.\\n\\nPhase 4 - Full enforcement:\\n- Enable a tenant onboarding flow in Console and APIs. Announce breaking change 30 days prior.\\n\\nRollback: Feature flag tram-enforce can be disabled globally to temporarily stop enforcement and revert to legacy routing.\\n\\nOperational readiness: runbook added to SRE playbook: 'tram-routing-failure' with steps to identify cache, policy_version mismatch, and circuit-break to legacy routing.\",\n  \"testing_plan\": \"Unit tests: policy evaluation, precedence rules, and schema validation.\\nIntegration tests: end-to-end decision path with mocked Tenant Policy Service, including cache miss, allowlist/denylist checks, and fallback behaviors.\\nE2E canary tests: route sample traffic for tenants with various TRAM configs and assert routing decisions satisfy residency constraints.\\nSecurity tests: penetration review for internal endpoints, ensure audit logs are tamper-evident.\\nPerformance tests: latency benchmark on routing/decide endpoint under 5k rps; ensure added median latency < 2ms.\\nQA checklist: verify header emission, audit log format, policy_version increments, and 403 response format for strict mode.\\nNOTE: Add test vectors for cross-border-consent header set/unset, and for tenant-level denylist entries (IP and route tags).\",\n  \"acceptance_criteria\": [\n    \"Edge can fetch TRAM for tenant and make routing decisions with <=2ms added latency on 95th percentile\",\n    \"Fallback_used telemetry increments and is visible in Console metrics when fallback occurs\",\n    \"Policy precedence enforced: denylist entries block specified routes regardless of other settings\",\n    \"Audit records for 100% of decisions are written to routing_audit and available for query\",\n    \"Canary mismatch rate < 0.05% before enabling strict mode for that cohort\"\n  ],\n  \"progress_updates\": [\n    \"2026-03-10 - Ticket created; initial spec drafted. Assigned to Marco Rivera.\",\n    \"2026-03-11 - Sync with Policy Service team; agreed on versioned TRAM schema and cache key format.\",\n    \"2026-03-12 - PoC for internal routing/decide endpoint implemented; basic residency predicate passes local tests.\",\n    \"Next - implement DB migration and add audit log writer; coordinate with Console team for header display and tenant UI.\"\n  ],\n  \"links\": [\n    \"https://confluence.redwood.ai/docs/TRAM-design-spec\",\n    \"https://github.com/redwood-inference/routing/pull/4523\",\n    \"https://dashboard.redwood.ai/metrics/routing-fallback-used\",\n    \"https://docs.redwood.ai/console/tenant-residency-guide\"\n  ],\n  \"notes\": [\n    \"Design trade-offs: storing full allowlist in cache increases memory but reduces policy-eval latency; we opted for an LRU sharded cache with tombstones for denies.\",\n    \"Consider exposing a dry-run mode in Console so customers can preview how their traffic would be routed under TRAM rules.\",\n    \"Need legal review for EU residency definitions (e.g., handling of non-EU data processors in EU-region deployments).\"\n  ],\n  \"title_field_name\": \"title\",\n  \"content_field_names\": [\n    \"description\",\n    \"spec\",\n    \"api_changes\",\n    \"data_model_changes\",\n    \"rollout_plan\",\n    \"testing_plan\",\n    \"acceptance_criteria\",\n    \"progress_updates\",\n    \"notes\"\n  ],\n  \"dataset_doc_uuid\": \"dsid_8bcf38423f3548078433c0dd4de38b36\"\n}",

      "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: EU Tenant Routing Authorization Matrix and Residency Enforcement\nSource: EnterpriseRAG/linear\nPath: /knowledge/company/sources/linear/engineering/ENG-100721-eu-tenant-routing-authorization-matrix.json\nConnector: linear\nWorkspace: engineering\nProject: geo-compliance-routing\nTeam: engineering\n\nregion + tier + model variant ) that satisfy legal / regulatory eu residency constraints and customer allowlist / denylist controls. spec : overview : we will add a tenant routing authorization matrix ( tram ) that is evaluated at request ingress and used by the smart routing engine. tram is tenant - scoped ( applies to org or project depending on tenant _ id ) and supports multiple policy axes : residency _ constraints ( enum : eu _ only, any _ region, region _ allowlist ), allowed _ tiers ( list : hosted, dedicated, private ), model _ variant _ preference ( map : role - > preferred _ variant ), and explicit _ customer _ allow / deny lists for special routing exceptions. policy precedence : explicit denylist > tenant residency enforcement > per - route overrides ( if permitted ) > global defaults.",

      "ordinal": 3,
      "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: EU Tenant Routing Authorization Matrix and Residency Enforcement\nSource: EnterpriseRAG/linear\nPath: /knowledge/company/sources/linear/engineering/ENG-100721-eu-tenant-routing-authorization-matrix.json\nConnector: linear\nWorkspace: engineering\nProject: geo-compliance-routing\nTeam: engineering\n\nrouting decision flow ( high level ) : 1 ) ingress : request arrives with tenant _ id and metadata ( consent _ header, jurisdiction _ hint, route _ id ). 2 ) resolve tenant tram config from tenant - config cache ( fast - path ). if missing, call tenant policy service with cache miss metric. 3 ) evaluate compliance predicates : does request require eu residency? is tenant in eu - only mode? is the requested route marked as cross - border - allowed? 4 ) candidate pool selection : choose model variants and deployment regions matching allowed _ tiers and residency constraints. if no candidate satisfies strict residency, move to fallback policy ( see fallback section ). 5 ) authorization check : consult tenant - level allowlist / denylist for special customer exceptions ( ip / routing tags ). 6 ) final",

document.title: EU Tenant Routing Authorization Matrix and Residency Enforcement
document.content:
{
  "key": "ENG-100721",
  "team": "engineering",
  "title": "EU Tenant Routing Authorization Matrix and Residency Enforcement",
  "status": "In Progress",
  "priority": "P1",
  "created_at": "2026-03-10",
  "updated_at": "2026-03-12",
  "creator": "Aisha Patel",
  "assignee": "Marco Rivera",
  "project": "geo-compliance-routing",
  "cycle": "2026-W11",
  "estimate": "8",
  "due_date": "2026-03-28",
  "labels": [
    "geo-routing",
    "residency",
    "policy-engine",
    "privacy"
  ],
  "dependencies": [
    "ENG-52340",
    "ENG-81234"
  ],
  "customer_impact": "high",
  "release": "routing-2.4",
  "security_review_required": "true",
  "description": "Implement a tenant-scoped authorization matrix and enforcement layer that guarantees EU-only data residency and routing for customers that opt into or require EU restrictions. This ticket defines the policy precedence, tenant configuration schema, routing decision flow, runtime enforcement hooks, audit logging, and rollout strategy. The goal is to provide deterministic, auditable routing decisions (region + tier + model variant) that satisfy legal/regulatory EU residency constraints and customer allowlist/denylist controls.",
  "spec": "Overview:\nWe will add a Tenant Routing Authorization Matrix (TRAM) that is evaluated at request ingress and used by the Smart Routing engine. TRAM is tenant-scoped (applies to org or project depending on tenant_id) and supports multiple policy axes: residency_constraints (enum: eu_only, any_region, region_allowlist), allowed_tiers (list: hosted,dedicated,private), model_variant_preference (map: role->preferred_variant), and explicit_customer_allow/deny lists for special routing exceptions. Policy precedence: explicit denylist > tenant residency enforcement > per-route overrides (if permitted) > global defaults.\n\nRouting decision flow (high level):\n1) Ingress: request arrives with tenant_id and metadata (consent_header, jurisdiction_hint, route_id).\n2) Resolve tenant TRAM config from tenant-config cache (fast-path). If missing, call Tenant Policy Service with cache miss metric.\n3) Evaluate compliance predicates: does request require EU residency? Is tenant in EU-only mode? Is the requested route marked as cross-border-allowed?\n4) Candidate pool selection: choose model variants and deployment regions matching allowed_tiers and residency constraints. If no candidate satisfies strict residency, move to fallback policy (see fallback section).\n5) Authorization check: consult tenant-level allowlist/denylist for special customer exceptions (IP/routing tags).\n6) Finalize decision, annotate request trace, and forward to Serving Runtime via routing API.\n\nFallback policy:\n- Strict mode (tenant residency_constraints == eu_only AND fail_on_violation==true): reject request with 403 and audit log.\n- Soft mode (default): fallback to EU-compatible model variant in hosted or dedicated EU pool. If none available, route to degraded model with redaction tag and notify customer via header X-Redwood-Routing-Fallback. Telemetry increments fallback_used.\n\nPolicy update semantics:\n- TRAM updates are versioned. Each change creates a policy_version id.",
  "api_changes": "New endpoints and headers:\n- GET /v1/tenant/{tenant_id}/tram -> returns current TRAM config and policy_version.\n- POST /internal/routing/decide -> internal API used by edge to request decision; payload: {tenant_id, route_id, jurisdiction_hint, consent_header, preferred_zone}. Response: {decision_id, region, tier, model_variant, policy_version, reason}.\n- New response headers for routed requests: X-Redwood-Routing-Decision, X-Redwood-Policy-Version, X-Redwood-Routing-Fallback (when applicable).\nAuth: internal endpoints require mTLS and service-to-service JWT with scope: routing:decide.\nBackwards compatibility: default when tenant has no TRAM is legacy routing behavior; feature flag 'tram-enforce' will gate enforcement during rollout.",
  "data_model_changes": "Tenant config storage (KV store + DB index):\n- New table/collection 'tenant_tram' with columns (tenant_id, residency_constraints, allowed_tiers, model_variant_map, allowlist, denylist, fail_on_violation, policy_version, updated_by, updated_at).\n- Cache key: tram:{tenant_id}:{policy_version}.\n- Audit logs: each routing decision writes a compact audit record to routing_audit (decision_id, tenant_id, timestamp, decision, reason, policy_version, route_id, request_id).\nNote: Use existing config migration tooling; add DB migration script and store initial policy_version = 1 when creating TRAM entries.",
  "rollout_plan": "Phase 1 - Canaries (2 weeks):\n- Enable read-only TRAM on edge to record decisions and diffs; do not enforce. Collect mismatch_count metric.\n- Target 5% of tenants (low-risk) + 100% of EU-region traffic for visibility.\n\nPhase 2 - Soft enforcement (2 weeks):\n- Enable soft mode for 20% tenants. Fallback to EU-compatible variants and emit headers. Add customer notifications for impacted tenants.\n\nPhase 3 - Strict enforcement (gradual):\n- Opt-in tenants can flip to strict mode. After 1 month of low mismatch, enable strict mode for customers who have completed verification.\n\nPhase 4 - Full enforcement:\n- Enable a tenant onboarding flow in Console and APIs. Announce breaking change 30 days prior.\n\nRollback: Feature flag tram-enforce can be disabled globally to temporarily stop enforcement and revert to legacy routing.\n\nOperational readiness: runbook added to SRE playbook: 'tram-routing-failure' with steps to identify cache, policy_version mismatch, and circuit-break to legacy routing.",
  "testing_plan": "Unit tests: policy evaluation, precedence rules, and schema validation.\nIntegration tests: end-to-end decision path with mocked Tenant Policy Service, including cache miss, allowlist/denylist checks, and fallback behaviors.\nE2E canary tests: route sample traffic for tenants with various TRAM configs and assert routing decisions satisfy residency constraints.\nSecurity tests: penetration review for internal endpoints, ensure audit logs are tamper-evident.\nPerformance tests: latency benchmark on routing/decide endpoint under 5k rps; ensure added median latency < 2ms.\nQA checklist: verify header emission, audit log format, policy_version increments, and 403 response format for strict mode.\nNOTE: Add test vectors for cross-border-consent header set/unset, and for tenant-level denylist entries (IP and route tags).",
  "acceptance_criteria": [
    "Edge can fetch TRAM for tenant and make routing decisions with <=2ms added latency on 95th percentile",
    "Fallback_used telemetry increments and is visible in Console metrics when fallback occurs",
    "Policy precedence enforced: denylist entries block specified routes regardless of other settings",
    "Audit records for 100% of decisions are written to routing_audit and available for query",
    "Canary mismatch rate < 0.05% before enabling strict mode for that cohort"
  ],
  "progress_updates": [
    "2026-03-10 - Ticket created; initial spec drafted. Assigned to Marco Rivera.",
    "2026-03-11 - Sync with Policy Service team; agreed on versioned TRAM schema and cache key format.",
    "2026-03-12 - PoC for internal routing/decide endpoint implemented; basic residency predicate passes local tests.",
    "Next - implement DB migration and add audit log writer; coordinate with Console team for header display and tenant UI."
  ],
  "links": [
    "https://confluence.redwood.ai/docs/TRAM-design-spec",
    "https://github.com/redwood-inference/routing/pull/4523",
    "https://dashboard.redwood.ai/metrics/routing-fallback-used",
    "https://docs.redwood.ai/console/tenant-residency-guide"
  ],
  "notes": [
    "Design trade-offs: storing full allowlist in cache increases memory but reduces policy-eval latency; we opted for an LRU sharded cache with tombstones for denies.",
    "Consider exposing a dry-run mode in Console so customers can preview how their traffic would be routed under TRAM rules.",
    "Need legal review for EU residency definitions (e.g., handling of non-EU data processors in EU-region deployments)."
  ],
  "title_field_name": "title",
  "content_field_names": [
    "description",
    "spec",
    "api_changes",
    "data_model_changes",
    "rollout_plan",
    "testing_plan",
    "acceptance_criteria",
    "progress_updates",
    "notes"
  ],
  "dataset_doc_uuid": "dsid_8bcf38423f3548078433c0dd4de38b36"
}

    "path": "/knowledge/company/sources/linear/product-management/ENG-42157-geo-boundary-policy-hub.json",
    "title": "Geo Boundary Policy Hub: EU-restricted routing, tiered fallbacks, and customer allow/deny gates",
    "source": "EnterpriseRAG/linear",
    "content": "{\n  \"key\": \"ENG-42157\",\n  \"team\": \"engineering\",\n  \"title\": \"Geo Boundary Policy Hub: EU-restricted routing, tiered fallbacks, and customer allow/deny gates\",\n  \"status\": \"In Progress\",\n  \"priority\": \"P0\",\n  \"created_at\": \"2026-02-28\",\n  \"updated_at\": \"2026-03-14\",\n  \"creator\": \"Maya Chen\",\n  \"assignee\": \"Omar Patel\",\n  \"project\": \"smart-routing-policy-suite\",\n  \"cycle\": \"2026-W10\",\n  \"estimate\": \"8\",\n  \"due_date\": \"2026-03-28\",\n  \"labels\": [\n    \"geo-routing\",\n    \"compliance\",\n    \"eu-only\",\n    \"fallbacks\",\n    \"policy-engine\"\n  ],\n  \"dependencies\": [\n    \"ENG-31244\",\n    \"ENG-52340\"\n  ],\n  \"customer_impact\": \"high\",\n  \"release\": \"routing-2.3\",\n  \"security_review_required\": \"true\",\n  \"description\": \"Summary: Implement a central 'Geo Boundary Policy Hub' in the routing layer that enforces EU-only data residency gates, supports per-customer allowlists/denylists, and orchestrates tier-aware fallback model variants when the preferred capacity is unavailable. Goals: (1) provide a single policy evaluator that takes customer configuration, request metadata, and global compliance rules to produce a deterministic route decision; (2) support explicit customer overrides (allowlists/denylists) with audit trails; (3) ensure graceful degradation by mapping to pre-approved model variants by tier (dedicated -> hosted compatible variant -> quantized fallback) while preserving residency constraints. This ticket covers the policy schema, runtime evaluator, integration hooks for the router, and rollout strategy including canarying and monitoring.\",\n  \"acceptance_criteria\": [\n    \"Routing evaluator enforces EU-only residency for customers marked as 'eu_residency_required' and refuses to route outside EU regions unless an explicit, auditable customer allowlist exists.\",\n    \"Customer-level allowlist/denylist entries override default routing only when the configuration includes an approved justification and admin actor recorded in audit logs.\",\n    \"When preferred tier capacity is unavailable, router selects the correct fallback model variant according to policy mapping (preserves residency), and the request completes with documented fallback reason codes.\",\n    \"All routing decisions produce a structured audit record with fields: request_id, customer_id, policy_version, decision, rationale, resolved_region, resolved_model, and actor (if override).\",\n    \"End-to-end tests simulate cross-region failure and validate that EU customers never egress data to non-EU regions under default and allowlist-deny conditions.\",\n    \"Perf regression < 5% on 95th percentile latency for routing decision path under 5k rps with policy cache enabled.\",\n    \"Console UI shows per-customer routing policy summary and a timeline of recent routing decisions that can be filtered by reason code.\",\n    \"Security team completes the review and signs off the policy evaluator's threat model and audit retention plan.\"\n  ],\n  \"implementation_notes\": \"Design: introduce a small, deterministic policy DSL (YAML/JSON) describing constraints: region_constraints, tier_preferences, allowlist/denylist blocks, and fallback_map. Implement a compact policy evaluator library in the router service (Go) with an in-memory policy cache and a persistence layer in config-store (etcd). Policy precedence: explicit customer denylist -> customer allowlist -> org-level residency constraint -> global defaults. For fallback mapping, use a model-variant registry that lists region compatibility and tier mapping; the evaluator must consult registry and capacity signals from the capacity plane. Add a 'decision_code' taxonomy for observability (OK, EU_RESTRICTION, ALLOW_OVERRIDE, DENY_OVERRIDE, FALLBACK_TIER, NO_CAPACITY, EGRESS_BLOCKED).\\n\\nRuntime hooks: router calls evaluator with (customer_id, request_meta headers, model_hint, required_residency). Evaluator returns (resolve_region, model_variant, decision_code, audit_blob). Router logs the audit_blob to the audit sink and emits metrics: policy_decisions_total{decision_code}, decision_latency_ms, fallback_rate_by_tier.\\n\\nTesting: unit tests for DSL parser and precedence rules, integration tests that spin up a sandbox capacity plane and simulate capacity loss, e2e tests with synthetic customers in EU and non-EU groups. Add mutation tests to ensure incorrect policies are rejected at upload time.\\n\\nMigration: bulk-migration script to convert existing 'residency' flags to new policy objects; a compatibility layer to read legacy fields until all customers migrated. Backfill audit logs for last 90 days for customers flagged as 'eu_residency_required'.\",\n  \"rollout_plan\": \"Phase 1 (canary, 1% customers): Deploy evaluator behind feature-flag in router, enable policy cache, route only synthetic traffic and internal QA customers. Monitor decision metrics and audit log volume. Phase 2 (10% orgs): Open to a small set of pilot customers with EU residency needs; enable live routing but keep rollback ready. Phase 3 (GA): Flip feature flag for all customers after 2 weeks of stable metrics and security signoff. Provide a rollback toggle and emergency circuit-breaker that forces pre-policy behavior.\",\n  \"metrics_and_observability\": \"Emit counters for decision_code and histograms for evaluation latency; record a per-request span with tags: customer_id, region_resolved, fallback_used, policy_version. Add dashboard: 'Geo Policy Decisions' showing top decision codes, per-customer fallback rates, and daily audit log ingestion size. Add alert: fallback_rate_by_tier > 2% sustained for 30m or decision_latency_p99 > 50ms.\",\n  \"links\": [\n    \"https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Geo+Boundary+Policy+Hub+spec\",\n    \"https://github.com/redwood-inference/router/pulls/6123\",\n    \"https://github.com/redwood-inference/policy-dsl/pull/47\",\n    \"https://docs.redwood.ai/ops/audit-log-schema#routing-decisions\"\n  ],\n  \"security_considerations\": \"Policy decisions are sensitive: do not include full request payloads in audit logs. Store audit blobs with only identifiers and hashed headers. Ensure audit sink supports customer-side retention controls for EU-residency customers and keys are managed via KMS. Mark this feature for mandatory security review and include threat model that covers malicious allowlist injection and replay attacks.\",\n  \"qa_notes\": \"QA should run the e2e scenario matrix: (EU customer with dedicated capacity) x (dedicated up/down) x (allowlist present/absent) x (denylist present/absent) and validate outcomes. Validate audit logs contain actor and decision_code. Validate console UI shows policy summary and recent decisions for sample customers.\",\n  \"comments\": [\n    \"2026-03-01 - Maya Chen: Initial triage and scoping complete. Proposed DSL attached to Confluence. Marked as P0 due to regulatory importance.\",\n    \"2026-03-04 - Omar Patel: Implemented evaluator prototype and unit tests. Pushed router hook branch, pending PR review. (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/router/pulls/6123)\",\n    \"2026-03-07 - Product (Elena Ruiz): Confirmed product acceptance criteria and requested console integration to show per-customer override rationale.\",\n    \"2026-03-10 - Security (Ravi Sharma): Requesting data-minimization in audit blobs and KMS key usage for audit retention. Security review scheduled 2026-03-12.\",\n    \"2026-03-12 - QA (Nikita Verma): Added e2e test matrix and created synthetic EU customers for canary tests.\",\n    \"2026-03-13 - Omar Patel: Canary rollout started for internal pilot customers. Monitoring initial metrics; fallback_rate_by_tier=0.8%.\",\n    \"2026-03-14 - Maya Chen: Security signoff added to links after review; leaving ticket In Progress to complete migration scripts and console bits.\"\n  ],\n  \"original_location\": \"linear/engineering/ENG-42157-geo-boundary-policy-hub.json\",\n  \"title_field_name\": \"title\",\n  \"content_field_names\": [\n    \"description\",\n    \"acceptance_criteria\",\n    \"implementation_notes\",\n    \"rollout_plan\",\n    \"metrics_and_observability\",\n    \"security_considerations\",\n    \"qa_notes\",\n    \"comments\"\n  ],\n  \"dataset_doc_uuid\": \"dsid_55b9ac7c77294d39bdd45108b052550d\"\n}",

      "ordinal": 5,
      "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: Geo Boundary Policy Hub: EU-restricted routing, tiered fallbacks, and customer allow/deny gates\nSource: EnterpriseRAG/linear\nPath: /knowledge/company/sources/linear/product-management/ENG-42157-geo-boundary-policy-hub.json\nConnector: linear\nWorkspace: product-management\nProject: smart-routing-policy-suite\nTeam: engineering\n\n- routing evaluator enforces eu - only residency for customers marked as ' eu _ residency _ required ' and refuses to route outside eu regions unless an explicit, auditable customer allowlist exists. - customer - level allowlist / denylist entries override default routing only when the configuration includes an approved justification and admin actor recorded in audit logs. - when preferred tier capacity is unavailable, router selects the correct fallback model variant according to policy mapping ( preserves residency ), and the request completes with documented fallback reason codes. - all routing decisions produce a structured audit record with fields : request _ id, customer _ id, policy _ version, decision, rationale, resolved _ region, resolved _ model, and actor ( if override ). - end -",

document.content:
{
  "key": "ENG-42157",
  "team": "engineering",
  "title": "Geo Boundary Policy Hub: EU-restricted routing, tiered fallbacks, and customer allow/deny gates",
  "status": "In Progress",
  "priority": "P0",
  "created_at": "2026-02-28",
  "updated_at": "2026-03-14",
  "creator": "Maya Chen",
  "assignee": "Omar Patel",
  "project": "smart-routing-policy-suite",
  "cycle": "2026-W10",
  "estimate": "8",
  "due_date": "2026-03-28",
  "labels": [
    "geo-routing",
    "compliance",
    "eu-only",
    "fallbacks",
    "policy-engine"
  ],
  "dependencies": [
    "ENG-31244",
    "ENG-52340"
  ],
  "customer_impact": "high",
  "release": "routing-2.3",
  "security_review_required": "true",
  "description": "Summary: Implement a central 'Geo Boundary Policy Hub' in the routing layer that enforces EU-only data residency gates, supports per-customer allowlists/denylists, and orchestrates tier-aware fallback model variants when the preferred capacity is unavailable. Goals: (1) provide a single policy evaluator that takes customer configuration, request metadata, and global compliance rules to produce a deterministic route decision; (2) support explicit customer overrides (allowlists/denylists) with audit trails; (3) ensure graceful degradation by mapping to pre-approved model variants by tier (dedicated -> hosted compatible variant -> quantized fallback) while preserving residency constraints. This ticket covers the policy schema, runtime evaluator, integration hooks for the router, and rollout strategy including canarying and monitoring.",
  "acceptance_criteria": [
    "Routing evaluator enforces EU-only residency for customers marked as 'eu_residency_required' and refuses to route outside EU regions unless an explicit, auditable customer allowlist exists.",
    "Customer-level allowlist/denylist entries override default routing only when the configuration includes an approved justification and admin actor recorded in audit logs.",
    "When preferred tier capacity is unavailable, router selects the correct fallback model variant according to policy mapping (preserves residency), and the request completes with documented fallback reason codes.",
    "All routing decisions produce a structured audit record with fields: request_id, customer_id, policy_version, decision, rationale, resolved_region, resolved_model, and actor (if override).",
    "End-to-end tests simulate cross-region failure and validate that EU customers never egress data to non-EU regions under default and allowlist-deny conditions.",
    "Perf regression < 5% on 95th percentile latency for routing decision path under 5k rps with policy cache enabled.",
    "Console UI shows per-customer routing policy summary and a timeline of recent routing decisions that can be filtered by reason code.",
    "Security team completes the review and signs off the policy evaluator's threat model and audit retention plan."
  ],
  "implementation_notes": "Design: introduce a small, deterministic policy DSL (YAML/JSON) describing constraints: region_constraints, tier_preferences, allowlist/denylist blocks, and fallback_map. Implement a compact policy evaluator library in the router service (Go) with an in-memory policy cache and a persistence layer in config-store (etcd). Policy precedence: explicit customer denylist -> customer allowlist -> org-level residency constraint -> global defaults. For fallback mapping, use a model-variant registry that lists region compatibility and tier mapping; the evaluator must consult registry and capacity signals from the capacity plane. Add a 'decision_code' taxonomy for observability (OK, EU_RESTRICTION, ALLOW_OVERRIDE, DENY_OVERRIDE, FALLBACK_TIER, NO_CAPACITY, EGRESS_BLOCKED).\n\nRuntime hooks: router calls evaluator with (customer_id, request_meta headers, model_hint, required_residency). Evaluator returns (resolve_region, model_variant, decision_code, audit_blob). Router logs the audit_blob to the audit sink and emits metrics: policy_decisions_total{decision_code}, decision_latency_ms, fallback_rate_by_tier.\n\nTesting: unit tests for DSL parser and precedence rules, integration tests that spin up a sandbox capacity plane and simulate capacity loss, e2e tests with synthetic customers in EU and non-EU groups. Add mutation tests to ensure incorrect policies are rejected at upload time.\n\nMigration: bulk-migration script to convert existing 'residency' flags to new policy objects; a compatibility layer to read legacy fields until all customers migrated. Backfill audit logs for last 90 days for customers flagged as 'eu_residency_required'.",
  "rollout_plan": "Phase 1 (canary, 1% customers): Deploy evaluator behind feature-flag in router, enable policy cache, route only synthetic traffic and internal QA customers. Monitor decision metrics and audit log volume. Phase 2 (10% orgs): Open to a small set of pilot customers with EU residency needs; enable live routing but keep rollback ready. Phase 3 (GA): Flip feature flag for all customers after 2 weeks of stable metrics and security signoff. Provide a rollback toggle and emergency circuit-breaker that forces pre-policy behavior.",
  "metrics_and_observability": "Emit counters for decision_code and histograms for evaluation latency; record a per-request span with tags: customer_id, region_resolved, fallback_used, policy_version. Add dashboard: 'Geo Policy Decisions' showing top decision codes, per-customer fallback rates, and daily audit log ingestion size. Add alert: fallback_rate_by_tier > 2% sustained for 30m or decision_latency_p99 > 50ms.",
  "links": [
    "https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Geo+Boundary+Policy+Hub+spec",
    "https://github.com/redwood-inference/router/pulls/6123",
    "https://github.com/redwood-inference/policy-dsl/pull/47",
    "https://docs.redwood.ai/ops/audit-log-schema#routing-decisions"
  ],
  "security_considerations": "Policy decisions are sensitive: do not include full request payloads in audit logs. Store audit blobs with only identifiers and hashed headers. Ensure audit sink supports customer-side retention controls for EU-residency customers and keys are managed via KMS. Mark this feature for mandatory security review and include threat model that covers malicious allowlist injection and replay attacks.",
  "qa_notes": "QA should run the e2e scenario matrix: (EU customer with dedicated capacity) x (dedicated up/down) x (allowlist present/absent) x (denylist present/absent) and validate outcomes. Validate audit logs contain actor and decision_code. Validate console UI shows policy summary and recent decisions for sample customers.",
  "comments": [
    "2026-03-01 - Maya Chen: Initial triage and scoping complete. Proposed DSL attached to Confluence. Marked as P0 due to regulatory importance.",
    "2026-03-04 - Omar Patel: Implemented evaluator prototype and unit tests. Pushed router hook branch, pending PR review. (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/router/pulls/6123)",
    "2026-03-07 - Product (Elena Ruiz): Confirmed product acceptance criteria and requested console integration to show per-customer override rationale.",
    "2026-03-10 - Security (Ravi Sharma): Requesting data-minimization in audit blobs and KMS key usage for audit retention. Security review scheduled 2026-03-12.",
    "2026-03-12 - QA (Nikita Verma): Added e2e test matrix and created synthetic EU customers for canary tests.",
    "2026-03-13 - Omar Patel: Canary rollout started for internal pilot customers. Monitoring initial metrics; fallback_rate_by_tier=0.8%.",
    "2026-03-14 - Maya Chen: Security signoff added to links after review; leaving ticket In Progress to complete migration scripts and console bits."
  ],
  "original_location": "linear/engineering/ENG-42157-geo-boundary-policy-hub.json",
  "title_field_name": "title",
  "content_field_names": [
    "description",
    "acceptance_criteria",
    "implementation_notes",
    "rollout_plan",
    "metrics_and_observability",
    "security_considerations",
    "qa_notes",
    "comments"
  ],
  "dataset_doc_uuid": "dsid_55b9ac7c77294d39bdd45108b052550d"
}

{
  "document": {
    "id": "dsid_83fa9cbbc1a445e3aaacdce1f9e0d786",
    "path": "/knowledge/company/sources/slack/eng-security/1719401234-mrk-cross-account-failover-questions.json",
    "title": "eng-security",
    "source": "EnterpriseRAG/slack",
    "content": "{\n  \"channel\": \"eng-security\",\n  \"thread_ts\": \"1719401234\",\n  \"first_message_ts\": \"1719401234\",\n  \"last_message_ts\": \"1719402920\",\n  \"participants\": [\n    \"jenna_prodsec\",\n    \"raj_infra\",\n    \"chris_sre\",\n    \"eva_security\",\n    \"kms-bot\"\n  ],\n  \"messages\": \"jenna_prodsec: Quick question \\u2014 we're designing regional failover for Private deploys using AWS KMS multi-region keys (MRKs). If us-east-1 primary goes down and we failover to eu-west-1 replica, what's required to ensure ciphertext decryptability across accounts? @raj_infra any gotchas with cross-account grants?\\nraj_infra: Short answer: MRKs are fine but pay attention to which key was used to encrypt. A replica MRK has its own key id but supports Decrypt for ciphertexts created by other replicas if they're truly MRKs (same key material). You need to allow Decrypt on the replica key for the principal that originally encrypted, or use grants.\\nchris_sre: Follow-up: in cross-account case we usually create a role in the other account and add an explicit key policy or grant. Grants are easier for short-lived access. Remember grants are region-local so you need them on each replica.\\njenna_prodsec: When key rotation happens in MRKs, does rotation replicate? Will old ciphertexts still decrypt?\\nraj_infra: MRK rotation: when you rotate primary, KMS rotates the primary's key material and can replicate to replicas depending on setup. But KMS MRKs preserve ability to decrypt older ciphertexts because ciphertexts include key metadata; rotation only affects future encrypts. Old ciphertexts remain decryptable as long as key state isn't disabled/deleted.\\nchris_sre: Important operational note: scheduled deletion or DisableKey affects all replicas? Deleting a replica doesn't delete others. But scheduling deletion of a primary doesn't auto-propagate \\u2014 be careful. Always test key state transitions.\\neva_security: For envelope encryption: recommend encrypting data key with MRK in same region as the data plane. Store encrypted DEK alongside object and prefer re-encrypting DEK during failover if needed.\\njenna_prodsec: Any example IAM policy or grant snippet for cross-account decrypt on replica?\\nraj_infra: Example grant CLI: \\n```\\naws kms create-grant --key-id arn:aws:kms:eu-west-1:111122223333:key/abcd-... \\\\\\n --grantee-principal arn:aws:iam::444455556666:role/PrivateDataPlaneRole \\\\\\n --operations Decrypt,ReEncryptFrom,ReEncryptTo\\n```\\nNote: grant is per-key (per-replica). Also need kms:DescribeKey and kms:GetKeyPolicy perms.\\nchris_sre: Also watch for alias mapping: alias/aws/replica MRK doesnt auto-map in our config; ensure app's config resolves to correct regional ARN.\\nkms-bot: Reminder: cross-account grants expire on principal deletion. Use least privilege and audit. :rotating_light:\\neva_security: TL;DR: MRKs work for regional failover + cross-account if you: (1) replicate MRKs, (2) create per-replica grants/policies for cross-account roles, (3) keep key states healthy, (4) re-encrypt DEKs as part of failover if app can't resolve original key id.\\njenna_prodsec: Awesome, thanks. I'll draft runbook steps and a quick test plan. Anyone want to add a quick test case?\\nchris_sre: Add test: encrypt DEK in us-east-1 primary, attempt decrypt in eu-west-1 replica with and without grant. Document behavior.\\nraj_infra: I'll add CLI steps to the runbook.\\njenna_prodsec: Great, assigning follow-ups: @raj_infra runbook, @chris_sre test plan, @eva_security compliance check. :thumbsup:\",\n  \"title_field_name\": \"channel\",\n  \"content_field_names\": [\n    \"messages\"\n  ],\n  \"dataset_doc_uuid\": \"dsid_83fa9cbbc1a445e3aaacdce1f9e0d786\"\n}",

{
  "channel": "eng-security",
  "thread_ts": "1719401234",
  "first_message_ts": "1719401234",
  "last_message_ts": "1719402920",
  "participants": [
    "jenna_prodsec",
    "raj_infra",
    "chris_sre",
    "eva_security",
    "kms-bot"
  ],
  "messages": "jenna_prodsec: Quick question — we're designing regional failover for Private deploys using AWS KMS multi-region keys (MRKs). If us-east-1 primary goes down and we failover to eu-west-1 replica, what's required to ensure ciphertext decryptability across accounts? @raj_infra any gotchas with cross-account grants?
raj_infra: Short answer: MRKs are fine but pay attention to which key was used to encrypt. A replica MRK has its own key id but supports Decrypt for ciphertexts created by other replicas if they're truly MRKs (same key material). You need to allow Decrypt on the replica key for the principal that originally encrypted, or use grants.
chris_sre: Follow-up: in cross-account case we usually create a role in the other account and add an explicit key policy or grant. Grants are easier for short-lived access. Remember grants are region-local so you need them on each replica.
jenna_prodsec: When key rotation happens in MRKs, does rotation replicate? Will old ciphertexts still decrypt?
raj_infra: MRK rotation: when you rotate primary, KMS rotates the primary's key material and can replicate to replicas depending on setup. But KMS MRKs preserve ability to decrypt older ciphertexts because ciphertexts include key metadata; rotation only affects future encrypts. Old ciphertexts remain decryptable as long as key state isn't disabled/deleted.
chris_sre: Important operational note: scheduled deletion or DisableKey affects all replicas? Deleting a replica doesn't delete others. But scheduling deletion of a primary doesn't auto-propagate — be careful. Always test key state transitions.
eva_security: For envelope encryption: recommend encrypting data key with MRK in same region as the data plane. Store encrypted DEK alongside object and prefer re-encrypting DEK during failover if needed.
jenna_prodsec: Any example IAM policy or grant snippet for cross-account decrypt on replica?
raj_infra: Example grant CLI: 
```
aws kms create-grant --key-id arn:aws:kms:eu-west-1:111122223333:key/abcd-... \
 --grantee-principal arn:aws:iam::444455556666:role/PrivateDataPlaneRole \
 --operations Decrypt,ReEncryptFrom,ReEncryptTo
```
Note: grant is per-key (per-replica). Also need kms:DescribeKey and kms:GetKeyPolicy perms.
chris_sre: Also watch for alias mapping: alias/aws/replica MRK doesnt auto-map in our config; ensure app's config resolves to correct regional ARN.
kms-bot: Reminder: cross-account grants expire on principal deletion. Use least privilege and audit. :rotating_light:
eva_security: TL;DR: MRKs work for regional failover + cross-account if you: (1) replicate MRKs, (2) create per-replica grants/policies for cross-account roles, (3) keep key states healthy, (4) re-encrypt DEKs as part of failover if app can't resolve original key id.
jenna_prodsec: Awesome, thanks. I'll draft runbook steps and a quick test plan. Anyone want to add a quick test case?
chris_sre: Add test: encrypt DEK in us-east-1 primary, attempt decrypt in eu-west-1 replica with and without grant. Document behavior.
raj_infra: I'll add CLI steps to the runbook.
jenna_prodsec: Great, assigning follow-ups: @raj_infra runbook, @chris_sre test plan, @eva_security compliance check. :thumbsup:",

    "messages"
  ],

See PR-19824. Access: today = Support-provided export; Console export is planned but not yet generally available.\",\n    \"2026-01-16 13:02 PT \\u2014 Dev Patel: Confirming with Security guidance re: what customer can receive (PII/tenant identifiers). Also need to ensure sample includes only their tenant + any shared infrastructure identifiers are generalized.\",\n    \"2026-01-17 08:40 PT \\u2014 Dev Patel: Drafted response for Atlas Payments. Coordinating with Allison to generate export.\",\n    \"2026-01-23 09:20 PT \\u2014 Allison Grant: Generated export from event store for the requested window. Smart-routing fallback chose us-east-1 for requests marked region=EU. Sample log lines attached. Paging on-call now.\\n\\nlindsay: on it. can someone drop the link to the traffic sample?\\n\\nravi: grabbing logs now. looks like a recent routing policy change rolled at 2024-10-02T03:42:10Z that introduced a fallback group mapping 'eu->global' for model-variants.\\n\\nops-bot: Affected requests last 15m: 2,174; unique users: 12; PII flag count: 84. Top target region: us-east-1.\\n\\nlindsay: thanks @ravi and @ops-bot \\u2014 initial priority is stop any further cross-region fallbacks. plan: disable the smart-routing fallback policy and pin acme-eu to strict residency. ravi, can you take the kill switch?\\n\\nravi: doing. running:\\n```\\nredwoodctl routing policy disable --name smart-fallback-global-eu\\nredwoodctl customer set-residency --customer acct-871 --region eu-west-1 --strict\\n```\\n\\nravi: disabled fallback policy at 03:45:02Z. policy state: DISABLED.\\n\\nlindsay: confirm that new requests from acme-eu are being routed to eu-west-1 only?\\n\\nops-bot: policy change propagated to all edge routers by 03:45:12Z. Observability: immediate drop in us-east-1 traffic for acct-871 from 220rps -> 0rps within 20s for matching request signature.\\n\\nmaria_priv: quick legal check \\u2014 if PII has touched us-east-1 storage, we need to follow breach assessment even if transient. pls capture which requests hit which model instances and whether logs/payloads were persisted.\\n\\nsam_platform: digging into instance logs. early sign: the majority of affected requests hit a fallback model variant 'gptx-8b-compat' hosted in us-east-1. KV cache writeback is disabled for that variant, but request traces show some debug-level logs that might contain truncated prompts. I will audit storage buckets next.\\n\\npaul_support: reported customer visibility: acme reported increased latency and an internal alert at 03:44. They are asking if data left EU. we need a concise customer-facing statement.\\n\\nlindsay: agreed. immediate customer message: \\\"We detected routing policy mismatch that temporarily routed a subset of requests outside your selected region. We have disabled the fallback and are investigating whether any persisted data left the EU. We'll update within 3 hours.\\\" @paul_support can you send that?\\n\\npaul_support: posting now. copy to #cs-acme for tracking.\\n\\nravi: audit results so far:\\n- model instances touched in us-east-1: i-0a1b2c3d (gptx-8b-compat), i-0f1e2d3c (gptx-8b-compat)\\n- object store writes (last 24h) for acct-871 in us-east-1: 0\\n- temporary trace blobs flagged: 84 entries (transient, retained 15m), stored in ephemeral-logs (no replication).\\n\\nsam_platform: ephemeral-logs retention policy is 15m and logs are auto-purged. We verified no snapshots or long-term storage for those blobs.\\n\\nmaria_priv: we still need to assume potential exposure until we complete the full forensics. open an incident evidence package. include hashes of the ephemeral blobs before purge.\\n\\nlindsay: action items:\\n- ravi: collect instance-level forensic dump (read-only), preserve ephemeral-logs hashes. (ETA 1h)\\n- sam_platform: verify storage write paths and ensure no snapshots. (ETA 1h)\\n- maria_priv: prepare legal notification draft and escalation criteria. (ETA 2h)\\n- paul_support: customer comms and log timeline. (immediate)\\n- lindsay: follow-up and coordinate with infra-sre for rollback if needed.\\n\\nravi: starting read-only forensic snapshot command now:\\n```\\nredwoodctl forensic capture --instances i-0a1b2c3d,i-0f1e2d3c --mode readonly --output s3://incidents-preserve/1775001234/\\n```\\nCommand accepted, snapshot job id = fj-3391.\\n\\nops-bot: snapshot job fj-3391 started (03:52:09Z). Estimated time: 18m.\\n\\nsam_platform: confirmed no long-term S3 writes. lindsay: on it. can someone drop the link to the traffic sample?

ravi: grabbing logs now. looks like a recent routing policy change rolled at 2024-10-02T03:42:10Z that introduced a fallback group mapping 'eu->global' for model-variants.

ops-bot: Affected requests last 15m: 2,174; unique users: 12; PII flag count: 84. Top target region: us-east-1.

ravi: doing. running:
```
redwoodctl routing policy disable --name smart-fallback-global-eu
redwoodctl customer set-residency --customer acct-871 --region eu-west-1 --strict
```

ravi: disabled fallback policy at 03:45:02Z. policy state: DISABLED.

lindsay: confirm that new requests from acme-eu are being routed to eu-west-1 only?

ops-bot: policy change propagated to all edge routers by 03:45:12Z. Observability: immediate drop in us-east-1 traffic for acct-871 from 220rps -> 0rps within 20s for matching request signature.

maria_priv: quick legal check — if PII has touched us-east-1 storage, we need to follow breach assessment even if transient. pls capture which requests hit which model instances and whether logs/payloads were persisted.

KV cache writeback is disabled for that variant, but request traces show some debug-level logs that might contain truncated prompts. I will audit storage buckets next.

paul_support: reported customer visibility: acme reported increased latency and an internal alert at 03:44. They are asking if data left EU. we need a concise customer-facing statement.

lindsay: agreed. immediate customer message: "We detected routing policy mismatch that temporarily routed a subset of requests outside your selected region. We have disabled the fallback and are investigating whether any persisted data left the EU. We'll update within 3 hours." @paul_support can you send that?

paul_support: posting now. copy to #cs-acme for tracking.

ravi: audit results so far:
- model instances touched in us-east-1: i-0a1b2c3d (gptx-8b-compat), i-0f1e2d3c (gptx-8b-compat)
- object store writes (last 24h) for acct-871 in us-east-1: 0
- temporary trace blobs flagged: 84 entries (transient, retained 15m), stored in ephemeral-logs (no replication).

sam_platform: ephemeral-logs retention policy is 15m and logs are auto-purged. We verified no snapshots or long-term storage for those blobs.

maria_priv: we still need to assume potential exposure until we complete the full forensics. open an incident evidence package. include hashes of the ephemeral blobs before purge.

lindsay: action items:
- ravi: collect instance-level forensic dump (read-only), preserve ephemeral-logs hashes. (ETA 1h)
- sam_platform: verify storage write paths and ensure no snapshots. (ETA 1h)
- maria_priv: prepare legal notification draft and escalation criteria. (ETA 2h)
- paul_support: customer comms and log timeline. (immediate)
- lindsay: follow-up and coordinate with infra-sre for rollback if needed.

ravi: starting read-only forensic snapshot command now:
```
redwoodctl forensic capture --instances i-0a1b2c3d,i-0f1e2d3c --mode readonly --output s3://incidents-preserve/1775001234/
```
Command accepted, snapshot job id = fj-3391.

ops-bot: snapshot job fj-3391 started (03:52:09Z). Estimated time: 18m.

sam_platform: confirmed no long-term S3 writes. There is one autoscaler that had a misconfigured env var ROUTE_FALLBACK=global which caused the variant to accept cross-region requests. patching that now.

lindsay: good catch. we need a postmortem item to add e2e tests for ROUTE_FALLBACK per-deployment and customer residency enforced at routing edge.

maria_priv: draft legal notice ready. key lines: "We are conducting a forensic investigation; immediate mitigation steps have been taken; based on preliminary evidence we have no indication of data persisted in non-EU long-term storage. We will inform you within 3 hours or sooner." will send to leadership for sign-off.

paul_support: customer updated in thread, acme replied: "Appreciate the quick action. Please confirm within the hour if any persisted data left EU."

lindsay: estimated blast radius update: ~2k requests (past 15m) matched fallback signature, 84 transient blobs, no confirmed persisted writes. severity remains SEV2 until forensics complete.

ops-bot: monitoring rule created: residency-violation-watch-acct-871. alert if any traffic to non-eu regions observed for acct-871.

ravi: forensic snapshot complete (04:11:02Z). uploading to secure bucket s3://incidents-preserve/1775001234/ completed. hashes: [sha256:3a7f..., sha256:9b1c...].

sam_platform: patched autoscaler env var and deployed a fix to edge routing to enforce per-customer residency at the edge (no fallback permitted). rollout completed 04:18:44Z to 3 regions.

maria_priv: legal sign-off received. recommendation: notify regulators if any persisted PII confirmed; for now communicate containment and ongoing investigation.

lindsay: next steps: create postmortem ticket, assign owners for remediation actions (tests, infra guardrails, monitoring), schedule follow-up with acme in 2 hours. handing off to next oncall @ravi for follow-through. I will join the follow-up sync.

ravi: acknowledged, taking handoff. I'll run a final sweep for any lingering non-eu traffic and validate alerting thresholds.
