# EU residency interview notes (private, provisional)

Owner: Jada Williams
Date: 2026-08-16
Status: Working notes only. Do not index or publish.

## Provisional synthesis

- Hosted API can pin customer inputs, outputs, persistent metadata, and audit logs to an EU region, while the hosted control plane remains global unless the customer uses a Private/Dedicated arrangement that contractually locates it in-region.
- Default fallback should be fail-closed: queue for a configured interval, use an approved EU-resident compatible model, or deny. Never infer consent from severity, availability pressure, a support request, or a global routing default.
- Cross-region processing/temporary replication needs prior written consent or an executed SLA exception, with scope, destinations, duration, and approver recorded.
- KMS selection must resolve a region-specific full key ARN (or explicit region-to-ARN map); aliases are regional. Failover requires healthy replica key state, grants/policies in the target region, and a decrypt test.
- Every decision needs structured audit fields. Retention defaults and the exact customer export SLA remain insufficiently reconciled across sources.
- Incident precedent shows that a global fallback environment variable can bypass intent; edge enforcement, monitoring, immediate disablement, evidence preservation, legal/privacy review, and qualified customer messaging are required.

## Interview questions still open

1. What is the authoritative hosted audit-event retention period and customer export delivery SLA?
2. Which hosted control-plane metadata is outside the EU, and is any of it Customer Data under each contract?
3. Is emergency failover without prior consent permitted in any standard Hosted API agreement, or only via an executed exception?
4. Are all supported EU failover pairs provisioned with KMS replicas/grants and tested continuously?
5. Who has final approval authority for enabling and ending an exception?

## Candidate support rule

Do not promise that data stayed in the EU until route, storage, trace, backup, KMS, and audit evidence is complete. State confirmed facts, containment, and the next update time; engage incident command, Security/Privacy, Legal, and the account owner for any unexpected or unapproved non-EU route.

# Hosted API EU Residency Failover

Owner: Platform Engineering (Jada Williams)
Audience: Customer Support, SRE, Security/Privacy, Legal, Account teams
Reviewed: 2026-08-16

## Purpose

This runbook reconciles the Hosted API EU-residency commitment with routing, KMS, audit, and support controls. It applies to EU-tagged Hosted API tenants. Customer-specific agreements and executed SLA exceptions override this general procedure; if terms cannot be verified, fail closed and escalate.

## Contract boundary

“EU-resident Customer Data” covers customer inputs, generated outputs, and persistent metadata stored in the EU region selected at onboarding. Hosted storage can be region-pinned. The Hosted control plane is global by default and may be outside the EU; Private or Dedicated deployments may contractually place it in an EU customer environment or region. Cross-region processing or temporary replication is allowed only with the customer’s prior written consent or an executed SLA exception. Regional KMS requirements apply when the customer supplies or configures regional key management. [FinServ finalized residency playbook, dsid_2b023bf742d74ad598bc190502d98808](/knowledge/company/sources/gmail/priya_natarajan/20260712-region-residency-constraints-and-fallback-playbook.json)

Do not describe “EU residency” as covering the global Hosted control plane unless the customer’s executed agreement explicitly says so. Do not treat an incident as consent.

## Supported routing modes

| Mode | Behavior when preferred EU capacity is unavailable | Cross-border consent |
|---|---|---|
| Strict EU-only | Queue for the tenant’s configured wait, route to a policy-approved compatible model in an allowed EU region, or deny. Never route outside the EU. | Not applicable; non-EU is denied. |
| EU-preferred, EU fallback | Prefer the pinned EU region, then an allowlisted EU standby or EU-resident compatible model. Queue or deny if no allowed target remains. | Not required when all processing and state remain within the contract’s EU boundary. |
| EU-preferred, approved global standby | After EU options are exhausted, route only to the named pre-approved region/model and only while the documented exception is active. | Prior written consent or executed SLA exception required. |
| Dedicated/Private EU multi-AZ or warm standby | Use in-region capacity and customer-controlled network/KMS boundaries; no automatic Hosted or global fallback. | A separate written exception is required before leaving the deployment boundary. |

Policy precedence is: explicit denylist, tenant residency constraint, permitted per-route override, then global defaults. An allowlist entry is valid only with approved justification and recorded admin actor. Every fallback must preserve the tenant’s allowed tier/model/region tuple and emit a reason code. Customer-specific agreements and executed SLA exceptions override this general procedure; if terms cannot be verified, fail closed and escalate.\n\n## Contract boundary\n\n“EU-resident Customer Data” covers customer inputs, generated outputs, and persistent metadata stored in the EU region selected at onboarding. Hosted storage can be region-pinned. The Hosted control plane is global by default and may be outside the EU; Private or Dedicated deployments may contractually place it in an EU customer environment or region. Cross-region processing or temporary replication is allowed only with the customer’s prior written consent or an executed SLA exception. Regional KMS requirements apply when the customer supplies or configures regional key management.               "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: Hosted API EU Residency Failover\nSource: Redwood Inference Platform Engineering\nPath: /knowledge/runbooks/eu-residency-failover.md\nWorkspace: task/jada-eu-residency-failover-20260816\n\n/sources/gmail/priya_natarajan/20260712-region-residency-constraints-and-fallback-playbook.json)\n\nDo not describe “EU residency” as covering the global Hosted control plane unless the customer’s executed agreement explicitly says so. Do not treat an incident as consent.\n\n## Supported routing modes\n\n| Mode | Behavior when preferred EU capacity is unavailable | Cross-border consent |\n|---|---|---|\n| Strict EU-only | Queue for the tenant’s configured wait, route to a policy-approved compatible model in an allowed EU region, or deny. Never route outside the EU. | Not applicable; non-EU is denied. |\n| EU-preferred, EU fallback | Prefer the pinned EU region, then an allowlisted EU standby or EU-resident compatible model. Queue or deny if no allowed target remains. | Not required when all processing and state remain within the contract’s EU boundary. |\n| EU-preferred, approved global standby | After EU options are exhausted, route only to the named pre-approved region/model and only while the documented exception is active. | Prior written consent or executed SLA exception required. |\n| Dedicated/Private EU multi-AZ or warm standby | Use in-region capacity and customer-controlled network/KMS boundaries; no automatic Hosted or global fallback. | A separate written exception is required before leaving the deployment boundary. |\n\nPolicy precedence is: explicit denylist, tenant residency constraint, permitted per-route override, then global defaults. An allowlist entry is valid only with approved justification and recorded admin actor. Every fallback must preserve the tenant’s allowed tier/model/region tuple and emit a reason code. [TRAM authorization matrix, dsid_8bcf38423f3548078433c0dd4de38b36](/knowledge/company/sources/linear/engineering/ENG-100721-eu-tenant-routing-authorization-matrix.json) [Geo Boundary Policy Hub, dsid_55b9ac7c77294d39bdd45108b052550d](/knowledge/company/sources/linear/product-management/ENG-42157-geo-boundary-policy-hub.json)\n\n### Consent and deny defaults",

Absence, ambiguity, expired approval, or inability to fetch the executed terms means deny non-EU routing.\n- Consent must identify tenant, allowed destination region(s), model/tier, data/state permitted to move, trigger, start/end or maximum duration, approver, and agreement or ticket reference.\n- Queue duration is tenant/contract specific.               "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: Hosted API EU Residency Failover\nSource: Redwood Inference Platform Engineering\nPath: /knowledge/runbooks/eu-residency-failover.md\nWorkspace: task/jada-eu-residency-failover-20260816\n\ndefault; do not quote 30 seconds unless it appears in the customer’s SOW.\n- Manual support approval, an incident severity, or a general availability objective cannot override an EU-only deny.\n- Roll back the exception when its end condition is met and verify no non-EU traffic remains.\n\n## KMS behavior\n\n1. Resolve the customer’s key for the actual processing/storage region using a full regional key ARN or an explicit region-to-ARN mapping. KMS aliases are regional and do not automatically map across replicas.\n2. Confirm the key state is healthy; required grants and key policies exist for the exact service/cross-account principal and key version; explicit denies have been checked.\n3. For multi-region keys, confirm the replica exists in the target region and that envelope metadata/dek handling can resolve or re-encrypt with the regional replica.\n4. Run a target-region encrypt/decrypt integration test before enabling traffic. A routing target without a successful KMS test is unavailable.\n5. Never move customer key material. For customer-managed keys, Redwood integrates with the region-scoped KMS/HSM; Private customers retain their keys. Log key ARN/region and policy/grant validation without logging secrets. [Multi-region KMS failover guidance, dsid_83fa9cbbc1a445e3aaacdce1f9e0d786](/knowledge/company/sources/slack/eng-security/1719401234-mrk-cross-account-failover-questions.json) [FinServ finalized residency playbook, dsid_2b023bf742d74ad598bc190502d98808](/knowledge/company/sources/gmail/priya_natarajan/20260712-region-residency-constraints-and-fallback-playbook.json)\n\n## Audit behavior",

Record configuration version and exception expiry for cross-border events. The policy design explicitly requires request_id, customer_id, policy_version, decision, rationale, resolved_region, resolved_model, and actor. [Geo Boundary Policy Hub, dsid_55b9ac7c77294d39bdd45108b052550d](/knowledge/company/sources/linear/product-management/ENG-42157-geo-boundary-policy-hub.json)\n\nKeep Hosted data-access audit logs in-region by default and use the customer’s approved regional export destination. Do not promise a particular retention period until the customer contract and current audit-retention policy are confirmed; the support evidence request records unresolved confirmation of the event schema and retention defaults.               "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: Hosted API EU Residency Failover\nSource: Redwood Inference Platform Engineering\nPath: /knowledge/runbooks/eu-residency-failover.md\nWorkspace: task/jada-eu-residency-failover-20260816\n\ndsid_ebc7b93e97384de09af72b95fab6e1b6](/knowledge/company/sources/slack/incidents/1775001234-oncall-residency-fallback-escalation.json)\n\n## Support response and escalation\n\nWhen a customer asks whether data left the EU:\n\n- Do not speculate or give an absolute assurance before evidence is complete.\n- State confirmed scope, current containment, whether processing versus persistence is confirmed, and the next update time.\n- Immediately disable any unapproved cross-region fallback and page incident command.\n- Preserve routing, instance, storage, trace, backup/snapshot, KMS, approval, and audit evidence; distinguish transient processing from durable persistence.\n- Engage Security/Privacy and Legal for any unexpected or unapproved non-EU processing, suspected payload/PII exposure, missing/expired consent, audit gaps, or inability to prove deletion/containment. Engage the account owner for contract interpretation.\n- Keep the incident open until a final sweep shows no disallowed traffic, persistence is assessed, evidence is approved for release, and customer/regulatory notification decisions are documented.\n\nReviewed support rule: **For an EU-tagged Hosted API tenant, treat cross-region routing as denied unless a current, customer-specific written consent or executed SLA exception authorizes the exact route. If an unexpected route occurs, contain first, preserve evidence, and tell the customer only what is verified—separating processing from persistence—on a stated update cadence.**\n\nThe incident precedent used a qualified customer statement, preserved evidence, involved Privacy/Legal, and withheld claims about persistence until forensics completed. [Residency fallback incident, dsid_ebc7b93e97384de09af72b95fab6e1b6](/knowledge/company/sources/slack/incidents/1775001234-oncall-residency-fallback-escalation.json)\n\n## Remaining uncertainty",

            "content_encoding": "utf-8",
            "content": "# EU residency interview notes (private, provisional)\n\nOwner: Jada Williams\nDate: 2026-08-16\nStatus: Working notes only. Do not index or publish.\n\n## Provisional synthesis\n\n- Hosted API can pin customer inputs, outputs, persistent metadata, and audit logs to an EU region, while the hosted control plane remains global unless the customer uses a Private/Dedicated arrangement that contractually locates it in-region.\n- Default fallback should be fail-closed: queue for a configured interval, use an approved EU-resident compatible model, or deny. Never infer consent from severity, availability pressure, a support request, or a global routing default.\n- Cross-region processing/temporary replication needs prior written consent or an executed SLA exception, with scope, destinations, duration, and approver recorded.\n- KMS selection must resolve a region-specific full key ARN (or explicit region-to-ARN map); aliases are regional. Failover requires healthy replica key state, grants/policies in the target region, and a decrypt test.\n- Every decision needs structured audit fields. Retention defaults and the exact customer export SLA remain insufficiently reconciled across sources.\n- Incident precedent shows that a global fallback environment variable can bypass intent; edge enforcement, monitoring, immediate disablement, evidence preservation, legal/privacy review, and qualified customer messaging are required.\n\n## Interview questions still open\n\n1. What is the authoritative hosted audit-event retention period and customer export delivery SLA?\n2. Which hosted control-plane metadata is outside the EU, and is any of it Customer Data under each contract?\n3. Is emergency failover without prior consent permitted in any standard Hosted API agreement, or only via an executed exception?\n4. Are all supported EU failover pairs provisioned with KMS replicas/grants and tested continuously?\n5. Who has final approval authority for enabling and ending an exception?\n\n## Candidate support rule\n\nDo not promise that data stayed in the EU until route, storage, trace, backup, KMS, and audit evidence is complete. State confirmed facts, containment, and the next update time; engage incident command, Security/Privacy, Legal, and the account owner for any unexpected or unapproved non-EU route.\n",

            "content": "# Hosted API EU Residency Failover\n\nOwner: Platform Engineering (Jada Williams)\nAudience: Customer Support, SRE, Security/Privacy, Legal, Account teams\nReviewed: 2026-08-16\n\n## Purpose\n\nThis runbook reconciles the Hosted API EU-residency commitment with routing, KMS, audit, and support controls. It applies to EU-tagged Hosted API tenants. Customer-specific agreements and executed SLA exceptions override this general procedure; if terms cannot be verified, fail closed and escalate.\n\n## Contract boundary\n\n“EU-resident Customer Data” covers customer inputs, generated outputs, and persistent metadata stored in the EU region selected at onboarding. Hosted storage can be region-pinned. The Hosted control plane is global by default and may be outside the EU; Private or Dedicated deployments may contractually place it in an EU customer environment or region. Cross-region processing or temporary replication is allowed only with the customer’s prior written consent or an executed SLA exception. Regional KMS requirements apply when the customer supplies or configures regional key management. [FinServ finalized residency playbook, dsid_2b023bf742d74ad598bc190502d98808](/knowledge/company/sources/gmail/priya_natarajan/20260712-region-residency-constraints-and-fallback-playbook.json)\n\nDo not describe “EU residency” as covering the global Hosted control plane unless the customer’s executed agreement explicitly says so. Do not treat an incident as consent.\n\n## Supported routing modes\n\n| Mode | Behavior when preferred EU capacity is unavailable | Cross-border consent |\n|---|---|---|\n| Strict EU-only | Queue for the tenant’s configured wait, route to a policy-approved compatible model in an allowed EU region, or deny. Never route outside the EU. | Not applicable; non-EU is denied. |\n| EU-preferred, EU fallback | Prefer the pinned EU region, then an allowlisted EU standby or EU-resident compatible model. Queue or deny if no allowed target remains. | Not required when all processing and state remain within the contract’s EU boundary. |\n| EU-preferred, approved global standby | After EU options are exhausted, route only to the named pre-approved region/model and only while the documented exception is active. | Prior written consent or executed SLA exception required. |\n| Dedicated/Private EU multi-AZ or warm standby | Use in-region capacity and customer-controlled network/KMS boundaries; no automatic Hosted or global fallback. | A separate written exception is required before leaving the deployment boundary. |\n\nPolicy precedence is: explicit denylist, tenant residency constraint, permitted per-route override, then global defaults. An allowlist entry is valid only with approved justification and recorded admin actor. Every fallback must preserve the tenant’s allowed tier/model/region tuple and emit a reason code. [TRAM authorization matrix, dsid_8bcf38423f3548078433c0dd4de38b36](/knowledge/company/sources/linear/engineering/ENG-100721-eu-tenant-routing-authorization-matrix.json) [Geo Boundary Policy Hub, dsid_55b9ac7c77294d39bdd45108b052550d](/knowledge/company/sources/linear/product-management/ENG-42157-geo-boundary-policy-hub.json)\n\n### Consent and deny defaults\n\n- Default to no cross-region consent. Absence, ambiguity, expired approval, or inability to fetch the executed terms means deny non-EU routing.\n- Consent must identify tenant, allowed destination region(s), model/tier, data/state permitted to move, trigger, start/end or maximum duration, approver, and agreement or ticket reference.\n- Queue duration is tenant/contract specific. The FinServ record proposes 30 seconds but does not establish a platform-wide default; do not quote 30 seconds unless it appears in the customer’s SOW.\n- Manual support approval, an incident severity, or a general availability objective cannot override an EU-only deny.\n- Roll back the exception when its end condition is met and verify no non-EU traffic remains.\n\n## KMS behavior\n\n1. Resolve the customer’s key for the actual processing/storage region using a full regional key ARN or an exp",

            "content": "licit region-to-ARN mapping. KMS aliases are regional and do not automatically map across replicas.\n2. Confirm the key state is healthy; required grants and key policies exist for the exact service/cross-account principal and key version; explicit denies have been checked.\n3. For multi-region keys, confirm the replica exists in the target region and that envelope metadata/dek handling can resolve or re-encrypt with the regional replica.\n4. Run a target-region encrypt/decrypt integration test before enabling traffic. A routing target without a successful KMS test is unavailable.\n5. Never move customer key material. For customer-managed keys, Redwood integrates with the region-scoped KMS/HSM; Private customers retain their keys. Log key ARN/region and policy/grant validation without logging secrets. [Multi-region KMS failover guidance, dsid_83fa9cbbc1a445e3aaacdce1f9e0d786](/knowledge/company/sources/slack/eng-security/1719401234-mrk-cross-account-failover-questions.json) [FinServ finalized residency playbook, dsid_2b023bf742d74ad598bc190502d98808](/knowledge/company/sources/gmail/priya_natarajan/20260712-region-residency-constraints-and-fallback-playbook.json)\n\n## Audit behavior\n\nEach route evaluation, recommendation, execution, rollback, denial, and override must produce an immutable structured record containing at least: request ID, customer/tenant ID, timestamp, policy version, decision, rationale/reason code, source and resolved region, resolved model/tier, override actor and approval reference (when present), and KMS region/key identifier. Record configuration version and exception expiry for cross-border events. The policy design explicitly requires request_id, customer_id, policy_version, decision, rationale, resolved_region, resolved_model, and actor. [Geo Boundary Policy Hub, dsid_55b9ac7c77294d39bdd45108b052550d](/knowledge/company/sources/linear/product-management/ENG-42157-geo-boundary-policy-hub.json)\n\nKeep Hosted data-access audit logs in-region by default and use the customer’s approved regional export destination. Cross-region audit replication for analytics is opt-in. Preserve incident evidence hashes and access-controlled forensic artifacts before transient data expires. Do not promise a particular retention period until the customer contract and current audit-retention policy are confirmed; the support evidence request records unresolved confirmation of the event schema and retention defaults. [Failover audit evidence request, dsid_5c1f084368874ecc9d633673048bc67f](/knowledge/company/sources/jira/customer-support/SUP-25444-region-failover-audit-log-request.json)\n\n## Validation\n\nBefore enabling or changing failover:\n\n1. Retrieve the executed residency terms, consent/exception, tenant policy, and expiry. Confirm the requested mode matches all four.\n2. Confirm denylist precedence and enumerate every allowed region, tier, and model variant. Ensure no global wildcard/default can bypass the tenant boundary.\n3. Simulate preferred-region exhaustion. Verify strict EU-only tenants queue, use an approved EU target, or fail closed.\n4. Test the exact target KMS ARN, grants, key policy, rotation/version behavior, and encrypt/decrypt path.\n5. Confirm route audit fields, override provenance, storage destination, trace/log destination, backup/snapshot behavior, and customer export destination.\n6. Exercise rollback and expiry. Verify the override is removed and monitoring observes zero disallowed routes.\n7. Attach redacted evidence to the change/incident ticket and record the validating engineer and time.\n\nAn incident showed that a misconfigured `ROUTE_FALLBACK=global` caused EU-tagged requests to reach us-east-1; mitigation required disabling fallback, edge enforcement, traffic sweeps, preservation of transient-log hashes, and monitoring. This is the negative test the validation must prevent. [Residency fallback incident, dsid_ebc7b93e97384de09af72b95fab6e1b6](/knowledge/company/sources/slack/incidents/1775001234-oncall-residency-fallback-escalation.json)\n\n## Support response and escalation\n\nWhen a customer asks wheth",

            "content": "er data left the EU:\n\n- Do not speculate or give an absolute assurance before evidence is complete.\n- State confirmed scope, current containment, whether processing versus persistence is confirmed, and the next update time.\n- Immediately disable any unapproved cross-region fallback and page incident command.\n- Preserve routing, instance, storage, trace, backup/snapshot, KMS, approval, and audit evidence; distinguish transient processing from durable persistence.\n- Engage Security/Privacy and Legal for any unexpected or unapproved non-EU processing, suspected payload/PII exposure, missing/expired consent, audit gaps, or inability to prove deletion/containment. Engage the account owner for contract interpretation.\n- Keep the incident open until a final sweep shows no disallowed traffic, persistence is assessed, evidence is approved for release, and customer/regulatory notification decisions are documented.\n\nReviewed support rule: **For an EU-tagged Hosted API tenant, treat cross-region routing as denied unless a current, customer-specific written consent or executed SLA exception authorizes the exact route. If an unexpected route occurs, contain first, preserve evidence, and tell the customer only what is verified—separating processing from persistence—on a stated update cadence.**\n\nThe incident precedent used a qualified customer statement, preserved evidence, involved Privacy/Legal, and withheld claims about persistence until forensics completed. [Residency fallback incident, dsid_ebc7b93e97384de09af72b95fab6e1b6](/knowledge/company/sources/slack/incidents/1775001234-oncall-residency-fallback-escalation.json)\n\n## Remaining uncertainty\n\n- The authoritative Hosted audit-log retention default and customer export delivery SLA are not settled by the reviewed sources.\n- Hosted control-plane metadata categories and whether a given contract defines them as Customer Data must be verified per agreement.\n- “Emergency failover per contract” is not blanket authorization; the evidence supports prior written consent or an executed exception, but older/customer-specific wording may differ.\n- Availability and readiness of every EU standby/KMS replica pair are not established here; validation is mandatory for the actual tenant and target.\n- Queue wait is contract-specific; 30 seconds appears only as a customer proposal, not a universal default.\n",

# Hosted API EU Residency Failover

Owner: Platform Engineering (Jada Williams)
Audience: Customer Support, SRE, Security/Privacy, Legal, Account teams
Reviewed: 2026-08-16

## Purpose

This runbook reconciles the Hosted API EU-residency commitment with routing, KMS, audit, and support controls. It applies to EU-tagged Hosted API tenants. Customer-specific agreements and executed SLA exceptions override this general procedure; if terms cannot be verified, fail closed and escalate.

## Contract boundary

“EU-resident Customer Data” covers customer inputs, generated outputs, and persistent metadata stored in the EU region selected at onboarding. Hosted storage can be region-pinned. The Hosted control plane is global by default and may be outside the EU; Private or Dedicated deployments may contractually place it in an EU customer environment or region. Cross-region processing or temporary replication is allowed only with the customer’s prior written consent or an executed SLA exception. Regional KMS requirements apply when the customer supplies or configures regional key management. [FinServ finalized residency playbook, dsid_2b023bf742d74ad598bc190502d98808](/knowledge/company/sources/gmail/priya_natarajan/20260712-region-residency-constraints-and-fallback-playbook.json)

Do not describe “EU residency” as covering the global Hosted control plane unless the customer’s executed agreement explicitly says so. Do not treat an incident as consent.

## Supported routing modes

Title: Hosted API EU Residency Failover
Source: Redwood Inference Platform Engineering
Path: /knowledge/runbooks/eu-residency-failover.md
Workspace: task/jada-eu-residency-failover-20260816

Do not describe “EU residency” as covering the global Hosted control plane unless the customer’s executed agreement explicitly says so. Do not treat an incident as consent.

## Supported routing modes

| Mode | Behavior when preferred EU capacity is unavailable | Cross-border consent |
|---|---|---|
| Strict EU-only | Queue for the tenant’s configured wait, route to a policy-approved compatible model in an allowed EU region, or deny. Never route outside the EU. | Not applicable; non-EU is denied. |
| EU-preferred, EU fallback | Prefer the pinned EU region, then an allowlisted EU standby or EU-resident compatible model. Queue or deny if no allowed target remains. | Not required when all processing and state remain within the contract’s EU boundary. |
| EU-preferred, approved global standby | After EU options are exhausted, route only to the named pre-approved region/model and only while the documented exception is active. | Prior written consent or executed SLA exception required. |
| Dedicated/Private EU multi-AZ or warm standby | Use in-region capacity and customer-controlled network/KMS boundaries; no automatic Hosted or global fallback. | A separate written exception is required before leaving the deployment boundary. |

Policy precedence is: explicit denylist, tenant residency constraint, permitted per-route override, then global defaults. An allowlist entry is valid only with approved justification and recorded admin actor. Every fallback must preserve the tenant’s allowed tier/model/region tuple and emit a reason code. [TRAM authorization matrix, dsid_8bcf38423f3548078433c0dd4de38b36](/knowledge/company/sources/linear/engineering/ENG-100721-eu-tenant-routing-authorization-matrix.json) [Geo Boundary Policy Hub, dsid_55b9ac7c77294d39bdd45108b052550d](/knowledge/company/sources/linear/product-management/ENG-42157-geo-boundary-policy-hub.json)

### Consent and deny defaults

### Consent and deny defaults

- Default to no cross-region consent. Absence, ambiguity, expired approval, or inability to fetch the executed terms means deny non-EU routing.
- Consent must identify tenant, allowed destination region(s), model/tier, data/state permitted to move, trigger, start/end or maximum duration, approver, and agreement or ticket reference.
- Queue duration is tenant/contract specific. The FinServ record proposes 30 seconds but does not establish a platform-wide default; do not quote 30 seconds unless it appears in the customer’s SOW.
- Manual support approval, an incident severity, or a general availability objective cannot override an EU-only deny.
- Roll back the exception when its end condition is met and verify no non-EU traffic remains.

## KMS behavior

[Document context]
Title: Hosted API EU Residency Failover
Source: Redwood Inference Platform Engineering
Path: /knowledge/runbooks/eu-residency-failover.md
Workspace: task/jada-eu-residency-failover-20260816

default; do not quote 30 seconds unless it appears in the customer’s SOW.
- Manual support approval, an incident severity, or a general availability objective cannot override an EU-only deny.
- Roll back the exception when its end condition is met and verify no non-EU traffic remains.

## KMS behavior

1. Resolve the customer’s key for the actual processing/storage region using a full regional key ARN or an explicit region-to-ARN mapping. KMS aliases are regional and do not automatically map across replicas.
2. Confirm the key state is healthy; required grants and key policies exist for the exact service/cross-account principal and key version; explicit denies have been checked.
3. For multi-region keys, confirm the replica exists in the target region and that envelope metadata/dek handling can resolve or re-encrypt with the regional replica.
4. Run a target-region encrypt/decrypt integration test before enabling traffic. A routing target without a successful KMS test is unavailable.
5. Never move customer key material. For customer-managed keys, Redwood integrates with the region-scoped KMS/HSM; Private customers retain their keys. Log key ARN/region and policy/grant validation without logging secrets. [Multi-region KMS failover guidance, dsid_83fa9cbbc1a445e3aaacdce1f9e0d786](/knowledge/company/sources/slack/eng-security/1719401234-mrk-cross-account-failover-questions.json) [FinServ finalized residency playbook, dsid_2b023bf742d74ad598bc190502d98808](/knowledge/company/sources/gmail/priya_natarajan/20260712-region-residency-constraints-and-fallback-playbook.json)

## Audit behavior

Source: Redwood Inference Platform Engineering

## Audit behavior

Each route evaluation, recommendation, execution, rollback, denial, and override must produce an immutable structured record containing at least: request ID, customer/tenant ID, timestamp, policy version, decision, rationale/reason code, source and resolved region, resolved model/tier, override actor and approval reference (when present), and KMS region/key identifier. Record configuration version and exception expiry for cross-border events. The policy design explicitly requires request_id, customer_id, policy_version, decision, rationale, resolved_region, resolved_model, and actor. [Geo Boundary Policy Hub, dsid_55b9ac7c77294d39bdd45108b052550d](/knowledge/company/sources/linear/product-management/ENG-42157-geo-boundary-policy-hub.json)

Keep Hosted data-access audit logs in-region by default and use the customer’s approved regional export destination. Cross-region audit replication for analytics is opt-in. Preserve incident evidence hashes and access-controlled forensic artifacts before transient data expires. Do not promise a particular retention period until the customer contract and current audit-retention policy are confirmed; the support evidence request records unresolved confirmation of the event schema and retention defaults. [Failover audit evidence request, dsid_5c1f084368874ecc9d633673048bc67f](/knowledge/company/sources/jira/customer-support/SUP-25444-region-failover-audit-log-request.json)

## Validation

Before enabling or changing failover:

Title: Hosted API EU Residency Failover
Source: Redwood Inference Platform Engineering
Path: /knowledge/runbooks/eu-residency-failover.md
Workspace: task/jada-eu-residency-failover-20260816

retention defaults. [Failover audit evidence request, dsid_5c1f084368874ecc9d633673048bc67f](/knowledge/company/sources/jira/customer-support/SUP-25444-region-failover-audit-log-request.json)

## Validation

Before enabling or changing failover:

1. Retrieve the executed residency terms, consent/exception, tenant policy, and expiry. Confirm the requested mode matches all four.
2. Confirm denylist precedence and enumerate every allowed region, tier, and model variant. Ensure no global wildcard/default can bypass the tenant boundary.
3. Simulate preferred-region exhaustion. Verify strict EU-only tenants queue, use an approved EU target, or fail closed.
4. Test the exact target KMS ARN, grants, key policy, rotation/version behavior, and encrypt/decrypt path.
5. Confirm route audit fields, override provenance, storage destination, trace/log destination, backup/snapshot behavior, and customer export destination.
6. Exercise rollback and expiry. Verify the override is removed and monitoring observes zero disallowed routes.
7. Attach redacted evidence to the change/incident ticket and record the validating engineer and time.

An incident showed that a misconfigured `ROUTE_FALLBACK=global` caused EU-tagged requests to reach us-east-1; mitigation required disabling fallback, edge enforcement, traffic sweeps, preservation of transient-log hashes, and monitoring. This is the negative test the validation must prevent. [Residency fallback incident, dsid_ebc7b93e97384de09af72b95fab6e1b6](/knowledge/company/sources/slack/incidents/1775001234-oncall-residency-fallback-escalation.json)

## Support response and escalation

When a customer asks whether data left the EU:

## Support response and escalation

When a customer asks whether data left the EU:

- Do not speculate or give an absolute assurance before evidence is complete.
- State confirmed scope, current containment, whether processing versus persistence is confirmed, and the next update time.
- Immediately disable any unapproved cross-region fallback and page incident command.
- Preserve routing, instance, storage, trace, backup/snapshot, KMS, approval, and audit evidence; distinguish transient processing from durable persistence.
- Engage Security/Privacy and Legal for any unexpected or unapproved non-EU processing, suspected payload/PII exposure, missing/expired consent, audit gaps, or inability to prove deletion/containment. Engage the account owner for contract interpretation.
- Keep the incident open until a final sweep shows no disallowed traffic, persistence is assessed, evidence is approved for release, and customer/regulatory notification decisions are documented.

Reviewed support rule: **For an EU-tagged Hosted API tenant, treat cross-region routing as denied unless a current, customer-specific written consent or executed SLA exception authorizes the exact route. If an unexpected route occurs, contain first, preserve evidence, and tell the customer only what is verified—separating processing from persistence—on a stated update cadence.**

The incident precedent used a qualified customer statement, preserved evidence, involved Privacy/Legal, and withheld claims about persistence until forensics completed. [Residency fallback incident, dsid_ebc7b93e97384de09af72b95fab6e1b6](/knowledge/company/sources/slack/incidents/1775001234-oncall-residency-fallback-escalation.json)

## Remaining uncertainty

[Document context]
Title: Hosted API EU Residency Failover
Source: Redwood Inference Platform Engineering
Path: /knowledge/runbooks/eu-residency-failover.md
Workspace: task/jada-eu-residency-failover-20260816

persistence until forensics completed. [Residency fallback incident, dsid_ebc7b93e97384de09af72b95fab6e1b6](/knowledge/company/sources/slack/incidents/1775001234-oncall-residency-fallback-escalation.json)

## Remaining uncertainty

- The authoritative Hosted audit-log retention default and customer export delivery SLA are not settled by the reviewed sources.
- Hosted control-plane metadata categories and whether a given contract defines them as Customer Data must be verified per agreement.
- “Emergency failover per contract” is not blanket authorization; the evidence supports prior written consent or an executed exception, but older/customer-specific wording may differ.
- Availability and readiness of every EU standby/KMS replica pair are not established here; validation is mandatory for the actual tenant and target.
- Queue wait is contract-specific; 30 seconds appears only as a customer proposal, not a universal default.

Before enabling or changing failover:

1. Retrieve the executed residency terms, consent/exception, tenant policy, and expiry. Confirm the requested mode matches all four.
2. Confirm denylist precedence and enumerate every allowed region, tier, and model variant. Ensure no global wildcard/default can bypass the tenant boundary.
3. Simulate preferred-region exhaustion. Verify strict EU-only tenants queue, use an approved EU target, or fail closed.
4. Test the exact target KMS ARN, grants, key policy, rotation/version behavior, and encrypt/decrypt path.
5. Confirm route audit fields, override provenance, storage destination, trace/log destination, backup/snapshot behavior, and customer export destination.
6. Exercise rollback and expiry. Verify the override is removed and monitoring observes zero disallowed routes.
7. Attach redacted evidence to the change/incident ticket and record the validating engineer and time.

An incident showed that a misconfigured `ROUTE_FALLBACK=global` caused EU-tagged requests to reach us-east-1; mitigation required disabling fallback, edge enforcement, traffic sweeps, preservation of transient-log hashes, and monitoring. Queue or deny if no allowed target remains. | Not required when all processing and state remain within the contract’s EU boundary. |\n| EU-preferred, approved global standby | After EU options are exhausted, route only to the named pre-approved region/model and only while the documented exception is active. | Prior written consent or executed SLA exception required. |\n| Dedicated/Private EU multi-AZ or warm standby | Use in-region capacity and customer-controlled network/KMS boundaries; no automatic Hosted or global fallback. | A separate written exception is required before leaving the deployment boundary. |\n\nPolicy precedence is: explicit denylist, tenant residency constraint, permitted per-route override, then global defaults.       "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: Hosted API EU Residency Failover\nSource: Redwood Inference Platform Engineering\nPath: /knowledge/runbooks/eu-residency-failover.md\nWorkspace: task/jada-eu-residency-failover-20260816\n\ndefault; do not quote 30 seconds unless it appears in the customer’s SOW.\n- Manual support approval, an incident severity, or a general availability objective cannot override an EU-only deny.\n- Roll back the exception when its end condition is met and verify no non-EU traffic remains.\n\n## KMS behavior\n\n1. Resolve the customer’s key for the actual processing/storage region using a full regional key ARN or an explicit region-to-ARN mapping. KMS aliases are regional and do not automatically map across replicas.\n2. Confirm the key state is healthy; required grants and key policies exist for the exact service/cross-account principal and key version; explicit denies have been checked.\n3. For multi-region keys, confirm the replica exists in the target region and that envelope metadata/dek handling can resolve or re-encrypt with the regional replica.\n4. Run a target-region encrypt/decrypt integration test before enabling traffic. A routing target without a successful KMS test is unavailable.\n5. Never move customer key material. For customer-managed keys, Redwood integrates with the region-scoped KMS/HSM; Private customers retain their keys. Log key ARN/region and policy/grant validation without logging secrets.       "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: Hosted API EU Residency Failover\nSource: Redwood Inference Platform Engineering\nPath: /knowledge/runbooks/eu-residency-failover.md\nWorkspace: task/jada-eu-residency-failover-20260816\n\nailover-questions.json) [FinServ finalized residency playbook, dsid_2b023bf742d74ad598bc190502d98808](/knowledge/company/sources/gmail/priya_natarajan/20260712-region-residency-constraints-and-fallback-playbook.json)\n\n## Audit behavior\n\nEach route evaluation, recommendation, execution, rollback, denial, and override must produce an immutable structured record containing at least: request ID, customer/tenant ID, timestamp, policy version, decision, rationale/reason code, source and resolved region, resolved model/tier, override actor and approval reference (when present), and KMS region/key identifier. Record configuration version and exception expiry for cross-border events. The policy design explicitly requires request_id, customer_id, policy_version, decision, rationale, resolved_region, resolved_model, and actor. [Geo Boundary Policy Hub, dsid_55b9ac7c77294d39bdd45108b052550d](/knowledge/company/sources/linear/product-management/ENG-42157-geo-boundary-policy-hub.json)\n\nKeep Hosted data-access audit logs in-region by default and use the customer’s approved regional export destination. Cross-region audit replication for analytics is opt-in. Preserve incident evidence hashes and access-controlled forensic artifacts before transient data expires. Do not promise a particular retention period until the customer contract and current audit-retention policy are confirmed; the support evidence request records unresolved confirmation of the event schema and retention defaults.       "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: Hosted API EU Residency Failover\nSource: Redwood Inference Platform Engineering\nPath: /knowledge/runbooks/eu-residency-failover.md\nWorkspace: task/jada-eu-residency-failover-20260816\n\nretention defaults. Retrieve the executed residency terms, consent/exception, tenant policy, and expiry. Confirm the requested mode matches all four.\n2. Confirm denylist precedence and enumerate every allowed region, tier, and model variant. Ensure no global wildcard/default can bypass the tenant boundary.\n3. Simulate preferred-region exhaustion. Verify strict EU-only tenants queue, use an approved EU target, or fail closed.\n4. Test the exact target KMS ARN, grants, key policy, rotation/version behavior, and encrypt/decrypt path.\n5. Confirm route audit fields, override provenance, storage destination, trace/log destination, backup/snapshot behavior, and customer export destination.\n6. Exercise rollback and expiry. Verify the override is removed and monitoring observes zero disallowed routes.\n7. Attach redacted evidence to the change/incident ticket and record the validating engineer and time.\n\nAn incident showed that a misconfigured `ROUTE_FALLBACK=global` caused EU-tagged requests to reach us-east-1; mitigation required disabling fallback, edge enforcement, traffic sweeps, preservation of transient-log hashes, and monitoring. document.title: Hosted API EU Residency Failover
document.content:
# Hosted API EU Residency Failover

Owner: Platform Engineering (Jada Williams)
Audience: Customer Support, SRE, Security/Privacy, Legal, Account teams
Reviewed: 2026-08-16

## Purpose

This runbook reconciles the Hosted API EU-residency commitment with routing, KMS, audit, and support controls. It applies to EU-tagged Hosted API tenants. Customer-specific agreements and executed SLA exceptions override this general procedure; if terms cannot be verified, fail closed and escalate.

## Contract boundary

“EU-resident Customer Data” covers customer inputs, generated outputs, and persistent metadata stored in the EU region selected at onboarding. Hosted storage can be region-pinned. The Hosted control plane is global by default and may be outside the EU; Private or Dedicated deployments may contractually place it in an EU customer environment or region. Cross-region processing or temporary replication is allowed only with the customer’s prior written consent or an executed SLA exception. Regional KMS requirements apply when the customer supplies or configures regional key management. [FinServ finalized residency playbook, dsid_2b023bf742d74ad598bc190502d98808](/knowledge/company/sources/gmail/priya_natarajan/20260712-region-residency-constraints-and-fallback-playbook.json)

Do not describe “EU residency” as covering the global Hosted control plane unless the customer’s executed agreement explicitly says so. Do not treat an incident as consent.

## Supported routing modes

| Mode | Behavior when preferred EU capacity is unavailable | Cross-border consent |
|---|---|---|
| Strict EU-only | Queue for the tenant’s configured wait, route to a policy-approved compatible model in an allowed EU region, or deny. Never route outside the EU. | Not applicable; non-EU is denied. |
| EU-preferred, EU fallback | Prefer the pinned EU region, then an allowlisted EU standby or EU-resident compatible model. Queue or deny if no allowed target remains. | Not required when all processing and state remain within the contract’s EU boundary. |
| EU-preferred, approved global standby | After EU options are exhausted, route only to the named pre-approved region/model and only while the documented exception is active. | Prior written consent or executed SLA exception required. |
| Dedicated/Private EU multi-AZ or warm standby | Use in-region capacity and customer-controlled network/KMS boundaries; no automatic Hosted or global fallback. | A separate written exception is required before leaving the deployment boundary. |

Policy precedence is: explicit denylist, tenant residency constraint, permitted per-route override, then global defaults. An allowlist entry is valid only with approved justification and recorded admin actor. Every fallback must preserve the tenant’s allowed tier/model/region tuple and emit a reason code. [TRAM authorization matrix, dsid_8bcf38423f3548078433c0dd4de38b36](/knowledge/company/sources/linear/engineering/ENG-100721-eu-tenant-routing-authorization-matrix.json) [Geo Boundary Policy Hub, dsid_55b9ac7c77294d39bdd45108b052550d](/knowledge/company/sources/linear/product-management/ENG-42157-geo-boundary-policy-hub.json)

### Consent and deny defaults

- Default to no cross-region consent. Absence, ambiguity, expired approval, or inability to fetch the executed terms means deny non-EU routing.
- Consent must identify tenant, allowed destination region(s), model/tier, data/state permitted to move, trigger, start/end or maximum duration, approver, and agreement or ticket reference.
- Queue duration is tenant/contract specific. The FinServ record proposes 30 seconds but does not establish a platform-wide default; do not quote 30 seconds unless it appears in the customer’s SOW.
- Manual support approval, an incident severity, or a general availability objective cannot override an EU-only deny.
- Roll back the exception when its end condition is met and verify no non-EU traffic remains.

## KMS behavior

1. Resolve the customer’s key for the actual processing/storage region using a full regional key ARN or an explicit region-to-ARN mapping. KMS aliases are regional and do not automatically map across replicas.

## Purpose

This runbook reconciles the Hosted API EU-residency commitment with routing, KMS, audit, and support controls. It applies to EU-tagged Hosted API tenants. Customer-specific agreements and executed SLA exceptions override this general procedure; if terms cannot be verified, fail closed and escalate.

## Contract boundary

“EU-resident Customer Data” covers customer inputs, generated outputs, and persistent metadata stored in the EU region selected at onboarding. Hosted storage can be region-pinned. The Hosted control plane is global by default and may be outside the EU; Private or Dedicated deployments may contractually place it in an EU customer environment or region. Cross-region processing or temporary replication is allowed only with the customer’s prior written consent or an executed SLA exception. Regional KMS requirements apply when the customer supplies or configures regional key management. ## Summary

For an EU-tagged Hosted API tenant, cross-region routing is denied unless current customer-specific written consent or an executed SLA exception authorizes the exact destination, model/tier, scope, trigger, and duration. If unexpected non-EU routing occurs, contain it, preserve routing/storage/trace/KMS/approval/audit evidence, separate processing from persistence, and communicate only verified facts on a stated update cadence while Incident Command, Security/Privacy, Legal, and the account owner review.
